incidents.root_cause: The profile denied exec by default and the fixture needed a setuid tool.
incidents.what: sandbox-exec refuses to exec any setuid binary, including ps, so the acceptance profile failed where the fixture used it to inspect processes.

incidents.title: Port validation tests lacked separate absent, zero and shared-port negatives and a positive callback control
incidents.rule: One negative per rejection reason, and a positive control in the same flow.
incidents.signature: One combined negative case passes for any of several unrelated reasons.
incidents.root_cause: Negatives were merged and the validator was never shown to accept a valid port.
incidents.what: Port validation was tested without distinct cases for an absent port, port zero and a port shared with another listener, and with no positive control in the same flow.

incidents.title: Browser-context isolation was mistaken for seed-state isolation
incidents.rule: Isolate each kind of state separately: browser state by context, data by reset and seed.
incidents.signature: A spec reads seed data while relying on a fresh browser context.
incidents.root_cause: Two different kinds of isolation were treated as one.
incidents.what: A spec read seed data and assumed isolation because each test had a fresh browser context, but database seed state is shared across contexts.

incidents.title: URL guards did not prove a test owned the disposable cluster, and shared state was not restored on failure
incidents.rule: Ownership comes from what the test created; restoration belongs in teardown that runs on failure.
incidents.signature: A test destroys or mutates state after checking only that the URL looks safe.
incidents.root_cause: A URL pattern shows what a target looks like, not who owns it.
incidents.what: URL guards were used as proof that a test owned a disposable cluster, and shared state was not restored when the test failed.

incidents.title: An acyclic declared dependency graph hid producer rows that an acceptance file needed
incidents.rule: An acyclic graph is necessary but not sufficient; derive edges from what each file requires.
incidents.signature: The dependency graph validates, yet an acceptance file needs a row that is not listed.
incidents.root_cause: Acyclicity was treated as completeness.
incidents.what: A declared dependency graph was acyclic, but an acceptance file still needed producer rows that were not declared.

incidents.title: A test reassignment written only in prose was not enforced by any tool
incidents.rule: Put a reassignment in one registry that every enforcing tool reads.
incidents.signature: A rule about which row owns a test exists in text, and tools disagree or ignore it.
incidents.root_cause: There was no single machine-readable source for the assignment.
incidents.what: A test reassignment was recorded only in prose, so the row selector, the activation diff check and the identity check could each read it differently or not at all.

incidents.title: A new test file was placed in a row whose activation order did not include a collection the file creates, and an oracle was asserted without its spec sentence
incidents.rule: Place tests by activation order and quote the spec before asserting.
incidents.signature: A test creates a collection or relies on a rule that the row order or spec does not support.
incidents.root_cause: Placement was chosen by topic and the oracle from memory.
incidents.what: A new test file was placed before the row that activates a collection the file creates, and an oracle was asserted without finding the exact spec sentence.

incidents.title: A later row overwrote a file that was already active
incidents.rule: Active files are append-only; later parts get new destinations.
incidents.signature: Part of a file must activate later, and activating it replaces the active file.
incidents.root_cause: The later part shared a destination with the earlier part.
incidents.what: Part of a file was due to activate at a later row, and the plan had that row overwrite the already active file.

incidents.title: A success control that forbade every connection pinned an implementation from before a later startup step that must connect
incidents.rule: Write prohibitions against the full startup contract, not the current implementation.
incidents.signature: A control test forbids all connections while a later row adds a startup step that connects.
incidents.root_cause: The prohibition was written for the current startup and not for the contract that later rows add.
incidents.what: A success control forbade every connection, which fixed the implementation as it was before a later startup step, such as a cleanup sweep, that has to connect. An engineer stopped on it.

incidents.title: A teammate could not run a destructive git command even when the lead instructed it
incidents.rule: Plan destructive operations for the context that holds the permission.
incidents.signature: A lead instructs a teammate to run a reset or similar, and the permission ceiling refuses it.
incidents.root_cause: The lead assumed an instruction overrides the sandbox rules of the delegated agent.
incidents.what: A teammate could not run a destructive git command such as reset --hard even when the lead told it to, because the tool permission ceiling wins over the instruction.

incidents.title: A process-group kill test used single-process stubs, so signalling the leader and the group looked the same
incidents.rule: A group-kill test needs a descendant, or it cannot tell group from leader.
incidents.signature: A group-kill test passes with stubs that have no descendants.
incidents.root_cause: The fixture had no descendant in the group.
incidents.what: A process-group kill test used single-process stubs, so killing only the leader and killing the whole group gave the same observable result.

incidents.title: A function signature named in the plan but never called by any test shipped ignoring its second argument
incidents.rule: Every planned parameter needs a test that makes it matter.
incidents.signature: The plan names a parameter that no test exercises.
incidents.root_cause: The signature belonged to a row whose tests never used it.
incidents.what: A function signature named in the plan had no test that called it with the second argument, so it could ship silently ignoring that argument.

incidents.title: Deleting PostgreSQL environment variables left client tools free to fall back to default host and port
incidents.rule: Pin the target explicitly; do not rely on removing the alternatives.
incidents.signature: A test clears PG variables to avoid the shared cluster, and a client tool uses its defaults.
incidents.root_cause: Absence of a variable was treated as safety.
incidents.what: Isolation was attempted by deleting PG environment variables, which let client tools fall back to default host and port instead of the owned cluster.

incidents.title: A timeout override was not re-checked against the newest ruling, and fixes were verified from the coverage note
incidents.rule: Verify from the code line, not from the note that describes it.
incidents.signature: A revision lands after a ruling and keeps an override that the ruling changed.
incidents.root_cause: The ruling and the revision were checked separately, and prose was trusted over code.
incidents.what: A revision that landed after a ruling kept a timeout override the ruling had changed, and fixes were confirmed from the coverage note rather than from the code.

incidents.title: A fail-closed URL rule copied into several helpers was not applied to every copy or every URL part
incidents.rule: One rule, every copy, every URL part.
incidents.signature: One helper checks the host and another omits the database or port.
incidents.root_cause: Copies drifted and the rule was applied to the part that was easiest to check.
incidents.what: A fail-closed URL rule was copied into several helpers, and not every copy applied it, nor to every URL part (host, database, port).

incidents.title: A UI test was accepted although no plan row owned a custom UI component it needed
incidents.rule: Every component a test needs has an owning row.
incidents.signature: A test drives a component that no row builds, so the last row meets a missing UI.
incidents.root_cause: Acceptance checked the test against the oracle and not against row ownership of its components.
incidents.what: A UI test needed a custom UI component that no plan row owned, so the last row would have met a missing UI.

incidents.title: A cross-row test needed setup absent from its own lifecycle, and green was claimed without a fresh-clone setup or a canonical temp directory
incidents.rule: Run from a clean state and compare resolved paths before reporting a pass.
incidents.signature: A test passes in a warm checkout and needs a database or path that the fresh lifecycle never creates.
incidents.root_cause: The test relied on state left by earlier work, and temp paths were compared unresolved.
incidents.what: A cross-row test needed a run database the harness should have created, and its setup was missing from its own lifecycle. Green was claimed before checking a fresh clone and a canonical temp directory with symlinks resolved.

incidents.title: HTTP-only timeouts were copied from a process-hang pattern without the reason
incidents.rule: An override without a stated reason is not reviewable.
incidents.signature: A timeout override appears in a test where its original cause does not apply.
incidents.root_cause: The override travelled without its reason, so nobody could judge whether it still applied.
incidents.what: Timeout overrides written for a process-hang pattern were copied into HTTP-only tests, with no record of why they were needed.

incidents.title: A control relied on state the test had changed earlier and silently became vacuous
incidents.rule: Place a control in the state it needs, and show it can change.
incidents.signature: A control that depends on a signed-in or seeded state runs after the test changed that state.
incidents.root_cause: The control was placed after a state change and was not compared against its own before state.
incidents.what: A control relied on state the test had altered earlier, such as a signed-out user, so it could no longer fail.

incidents.title: A rule set widened by tag survived dropping one tag because only some tags had a planted violation
incidents.rule: Every tag in a rule needs its own planted violation.
incidents.signature: A check covers several tags, and removing one tag leaves the suite green.
incidents.root_cause: Coverage of the rule set was assumed from the widened list.
incidents.what: A rule set was widened by tag, and without a planted violation for each tag, dropping a tag went unnoticed.

incidents.title: A second clone named after the remote held a stale tip and was mistaken for the working checkout
incidents.rule: Never identify a checkout by its folder name.
incidents.signature: Two checkouts exist, and the folder name suggests the wrong one is current.
incidents.root_cause: The checkout was identified by folder name, not by its HEAD commit.
incidents.what: After context compaction, a second clone named after the remote held a stale tip and could be mistaken for the working checkout.

incidents.title: Rows that point at a relationship target were ordered before the target was registered, tempting stubs or optional fields
incidents.rule: Fix the order, not the contract.
incidents.signature: A row needs a related record that a later row creates.
incidents.root_cause: Row order followed topic, not the relationship graph.
incidents.what: Rows were ordered so that a relationship target was registered after the row pointing at it, which pushed toward stubbed or optional fields.

incidents.title: Two validators enforcing the same rule masked single-file mutations
incidents.rule: Test every layer of a redundant check independently.
incidents.signature: Removing one of two redundant checks leaves the suite green.
incidents.root_cause: Redundancy was treated as extra safety and tested only as a pair.
incidents.what: Two validators enforced the same rule, so mutating either one alone was caught by the other and the gap was hidden. Entry points also lacked their own refusal rows.

incidents.title: Signalling a process group of only zombie members returned a permission error on macOS
incidents.rule: Repeat race-dependent cleanup tests; classify errors by what they mean for the target.
incidents.signature: Cleanup fails intermittently when the group has exited but not been reaped.
incidents.root_cause: The error code was read as a real denial instead of a gone group.
incidents.what: On macOS, signalling a process group whose members were all zombies could return a permission error, and cleanup treated it as a failure. The race showed only over repeated runs.

incidents.title: A reason regex matched text the test itself injected and missed the reason on the error line
incidents.rule: Anchor a reason match to the error line and keep injected text out of its reach.
incidents.signature: A refusal assertion passes because its pattern matches the test input.
incidents.root_cause: The pattern was broad and not anchored to the error output.
incidents.what: A reason regex matched text the test had injected, and did not require the reason on the same line as the error name.

incidents.title: A sandboxed HOME hid tool caches such as package-manager shims
incidents.rule: When replacing HOME, forward every cache the tools need and block fetching.
incidents.signature: A tool works normally and fails once HOME points at a temp directory.
incidents.root_cause: The cache location was derived from HOME and was not forwarded.
incidents.what: A sandboxed HOME hid tool caches, such as package-manager shims, so tools failed or tried to fetch.

incidents.title: A guard control asserted only exit 0, so a warn-and-pass guard looked like a clean pass
incidents.rule: Check output as well as exit status in a clean-pass control.
incidents.signature: A guard that prints an error but exits 0 passes a control that checks the exit code.
incidents.root_cause: Only the exit code was checked.
incidents.what: A guard control did not assert the absence of the error text, so a guard that warned and passed was indistinguishable from a clean pass.

incidents.title: A rule scoped to work after a ruling was applied per commit while one commit held old and new patterns
incidents.rule: Scope a rule by the file, not the commit that carries it.
incidents.signature: One commit contains files that predate the ruling and files that follow it.
incidents.root_cause: The scope was set per commit, not per file.
incidents.what: A rule scoped to work after a ruling was applied to a whole commit, but that commit held both old and new patterns.

incidents.title: A digest present anywhere in a manifest was taken as proof it belonged to its file
incidents.rule: Verify pairs, not membership.
incidents.signature: A check finds the digest somewhere in the manifest and passes.
incidents.root_cause: The check tested membership, not the path-to-digest pairing.
incidents.what: A digest present anywhere in a manifest did not prove it belonged to its file, so swapped or misplaced digests could pass.

incidents.title: After activation a registry line named a pending path that no longer existed, and a verifier flagged it
incidents.rule: A verifier must follow moves through history, not require the old path to exist.
incidents.signature: A verifier reports a missing path that was legitimately moved at activation.
incidents.root_cause: The verifier assumed paths in the registry always exist on disk.
incidents.what: After activation, a registry line named a pending path that no longer existed, and a verifier flagged it instead of following history.

incidents.title: A poll timeout placed in assertion options was still a propagation override, and shared helpers were left out of the dependent root verdict
incidents.rule: Only an oracle-valued deadline is exempt from the override rule; include shared helpers in each dependent verdict.
incidents.signature: A timeout override hides in assertion options or a shared helper that a root depends on.
incidents.root_cause: Only test-level timeouts were treated as overrides, and verdicts stopped at the root files.
incidents.what: A poll timeout in assertion options carried an override across a revision just like a test-level timeout. Shared helpers were not checked as part of each dependent root verdict.

incidents.title: A marker generator listing every earlier unmarked root made a root approved later repeat an old path that a later marker already held
incidents.rule: Check uniqueness across all markers, and re-read inputs immediately before reporting.
incidents.signature: Two markers name the same old path because a generator listed all earlier unmarked roots.
incidents.root_cause: Uniqueness of old paths was checked per marker, not globally, and the review folder was read once.
incidents.what: A marker generator listed every earlier unmarked root, so an earlier root approved later could repeat an old path that a later marker already held. New verdicts could also land in the review folder just before reporting.

incidents.title: Test discovery was compared with an absolute scratch prefix that matched by accident, and guard omission mutants were not each killed
incidents.rule: Compare relative names and kill every mutant on its own.
incidents.signature: A discovery comparison passes because an absolute prefix coincidentally lines up.
incidents.root_cause: Paths were not normalized to relative filenames, and mutants were counted together.
incidents.what: Test discovery was compared using absolute paths, and an absolute scratch prefix matched by accident. Omission mutants of a guard were not each required to be killed independently.

incidents.title: A document already at its hard size cap had no room for the next transcription, so the cap was met only after editing
incidents.rule: Plan against a hard cap before the edit, not after.
incidents.signature: An edit is made first and the size cap is discovered afterward.
incidents.root_cause: The size limit was checked after the edit rather than planned.
incidents.what: A document sat 132 bytes under a hard size cap, so the next transcription had to start by moving history out. The cap was not budgeted before editing.

incidents.title: Finished work sat for hours because replies never arrived, the clock was misread and worktrees were not swept
incidents.rule: Sweep the disk and read a real clock before trusting replies.
incidents.signature: Several teammates finish, no reply arrives, and the lead waits.
incidents.root_cause: Progress was judged from replies and an assumed time instead of from disk and a real clock.
incidents.what: Seven teammates finished work and their replies never arrived. The lead read the clock wrong, assuming stamps from one hour when real time was hours later, and did not sweep worktrees, so finished roots sat about nine hours.

incidents.title: A syntax hygiene rule flagging every literal timer over one second also flagged a cancellation watchdog
incidents.rule: A hygiene rule should test intent, not only syntax.
incidents.signature: A rule against long timers rejects a bound that fails and is cleared.
incidents.root_cause: The rule matched surface syntax, not whether the timer is a sleep.
incidents.what: A hygiene rule that flagged every literal timer over one second also flagged a cancellation watchdog that bounds an awaited event.

incidents.title: An identity checker rejecting every shared destination across pending roots flagged inert drafts
incidents.rule: Enforce destination uniqueness where files become active.
incidents.signature: Two pending drafts name one destination and the checker fails.
incidents.root_cause: Uniqueness was enforced across all pending roots instead of at activation.
incidents.what: An identity checker rejected every shared destination across pending roots, which flagged inert drafts that were not active.

incidents.title: A stage hang deadline copied from a planning estimate killed a correct run once heavier tests joined
incidents.rule: Measure, then set deadlines.
incidents.signature: A stage that passed earlier is killed after more tests are added.
incidents.root_cause: The deadline came from an estimate, not from measurement.
incidents.what: A stage hang deadline copied from a planning estimate killed a correct run once heavier tests joined the stage.

incidents.title: Vitest 4 ran projects in parallel and file serialization inside a project did not order whole-cluster checks
incidents.rule: Serialize across projects explicitly when they share state.
incidents.signature: Inventory checks across a shared cluster race between projects.
incidents.root_cause: File serialization was assumed to apply across projects.
incidents.what: Vitest 4 runs projects in parallel unless a group order is set, and disabling file parallelism serializes only inside a project, so whole-cluster inventory checks raced.

incidents.title: A local guard behind a shared environment pin was masked, and a mutation claim was reasoned instead of measured
incidents.rule: Measure mutations and protect files first.
incidents.signature: Removing a guard changes nothing because an outer pin already covers it.
incidents.root_cause: Masking was not tested and mutations ran on unprotected files.
incidents.what: A local guard behind a shared environment pin was masked, so removing it changed nothing. The mutation claim was reasoned, not measured, and mutation scripts did not snapshot untracked copied files before mutating.

incidents.title: A QA case followed only 3xx redirects while Payload 3 admin redirects under Next 16 are soft redirects with HTTP 200
incidents.rule: Assert what the user sees, not the transport mechanism.
incidents.signature: A test expecting a 3xx fails on a correct redirect.
incidents.root_cause: The test assumed classic HTTP redirects.
incidents.what: Payload 3 admin redirects under Next 16 are RSC soft redirects with HTTP 200, so a QA case that followed only 3xx was stricter than its row. Next 16 also rewrites next-env.d.ts on every dev start.

incidents.title: A QA-template line pasted into an engineer task contradicted the engineer commit duty
incidents.rule: One template per role.
incidents.signature: A task carries an instruction from another role template.
incidents.root_cause: Templates for different roles were mixed in one brief.
incidents.what: A QA-template line, do not commit, was pasted into an engineer task and contradicted the engineer commit duty.

incidents.title: A cross-agent inventory flake came from sharing one harness cluster between runtime agents
incidents.rule: Give each agent its own cluster.
incidents.signature: Inventory checks fail when two agents use one cluster.
incidents.root_cause: Cluster ownership was per environment, not per agent.
incidents.what: A cross-agent inventory flake showed that two runtime agents shared one harness cluster.

incidents.title: A database adapter created an absent database even with schema push disabled
incidents.rule: Make a missing database fail by name instead of creating it.
incidents.signature: A misspelled or missing database name silently becomes a new empty database.
incidents.root_cause: The adapter default is to create the database on connect.
incidents.what: Payload 3 db-postgres created an absent database even with push false, so a missing database was not a failure.

incidents.title: A stage that kept a database alive collided with later inventory and frozen-clock gc cases
incidents.rule: Tie resource lifetime to its creating stage.
incidents.signature: A leftover database from one stage changes the result of a later stage.
incidents.root_cause: Database lifetime was not tied to the stage that created it.
incidents.what: A stage kept a database alive, which collided with later inventory or frozen-clock gc cases.

incidents.title: A readiness deadline tested only inside a step was untested outside it
incidents.rule: Test the deadline on every path that can reach it.
incidents.signature: A deadline is proven on one code path and ships on another.
incidents.root_cause: The test used the convenient path.
incidents.what: A readiness deadline was tested only inside a step, so the path outside a step had no test.

incidents.title: A known red was listed before checking the scan roots of the hygiene rule that raised it
incidents.rule: Confirm a rule scope before reporting its finding.
incidents.signature: A finding is recorded as a known failure without confirming the rule scans that file.
incidents.root_cause: The finding was trusted without confirming the rule scope.
incidents.what: A hygiene rule finding was listed as a known red before its scan roots were checked.

incidents.title: A static watchdog rule accepting only an inline await of a new promise flagged stored promises and other valid shapes
incidents.rule: Widen a rule by shape and prove it with near-miss negatives.
incidents.signature: A rule written against one syntax shape rejects equivalent valid code.
incidents.root_cause: The rule matched one shape instead of the intent.
incidents.what: A static watchdog rule that accepted only an inline await new Promise flagged stored promises, outer let handles, catch-reject-return branches and Playwright test.setTimeout.

incidents.title: A redirect test searching for one allowed substring accepted a bad target beside a benign decoy
incidents.rule: Validate all candidates, not the first acceptable one.
incidents.signature: A redirect check passes because one acceptable string appears among several candidates.
incidents.root_cause: The test looked for any match instead of validating every candidate.
incidents.what: A redirect test that searched for one allowed substring accepted a bad target placed beside a benign decoy, and hop bodies were not inspected.

incidents.title: Two branches implementing the same stage split were merged without re-measuring, although merged tests can change a project time several times over
incidents.rule: Re-measure after a merge that changes the tests in a stage.
incidents.signature: A merged stage split keeps timings measured before the merge.
incidents.root_cause: The base shape and timings came from the wrong branch.
incidents.what: When two branches implemented the same stage split, merged tests changed a project time several times over, so earlier measurements no longer applied.

incidents.title: Expected lifecycle refusals were mixed with static findings in a sweep
incidents.rule: Report expected refusals apart from real findings.
incidents.signature: A sweep report cannot tell an intended refusal from a real finding.
incidents.root_cause: Both kinds of output went to one list.
incidents.what: An N-02b sweep mixed expected lifecycle refusals with static findings.

incidents.title: A readiness check measured the lead checkout while preship measures the Foundry clone
incidents.rule: Check the tree the gate actually reads.
incidents.signature: A readiness verdict is taken from one checkout and the gate reads another.
incidents.root_cause: The checked tree and the measured tree were different.
incidents.what: Preship measures the Foundry clone, not the lead checkout, so a readiness check on the lead checkout said nothing about what preship would see.

incidents.title: A truncated FAST run stopped at the first red stage and understated the stage sum by about half
incidents.rule: Measure the complete run before claiming a budget.
incidents.signature: A timing taken from a run that stopped early is used as a full measurement.
incidents.root_cause: Time up to a failure was read as total time.
incidents.what: A FAST run that stopped at the first red stage understated the stage sum by about half, and was sold as a green preship measurement.

incidents.title: A moved history row was silently modernized instead of staying byte identical
incidents.rule: Separate source-preserving relocation from attributed status changes.
incidents.signature: A move that is described as byte identical changes a this version label.
incidents.root_cause: Relocation and status update were done in one edit.
incidents.what: A historical row moved between documents was updated to the current version label during a purported byte identical move.

incidents.title: ASCII-only fixtures could not tell UTF-16 code unit order from UTF-8 byte order
incidents.rule: Choose data that separates the alternatives under test.
incidents.signature: A sort or compare test passes under either ordering because all data is ASCII.
incidents.root_cause: The test data could not distinguish the two orderings.
incidents.what: Fixtures were ASCII only, so a comparison by UTF-16 order and one by UTF-8 byte order gave the same result.

incidents.title: Marker SHA, reviewer approval scope, successor closure and activation ownership were treated as one fact
incidents.rule: One fact per field.
incidents.signature: A marker is read as proof of approval, closure and ownership at once.
incidents.root_cause: One field was asked to carry four meanings.
incidents.what: An audit found that marker SHA, reviewer approval scope, successor closure and activation ownership are four different facts, and old-path edges must stay globally unique.

incidents.title: A missing independently callable guard lacked protocol cases, and macOS path aliases looked like regressions
incidents.rule: Resolve paths before comparing, and compare to the active bytes first.
incidents.signature: A guard without its own tests and cwd assertions failing on path aliases.
incidents.root_cause: Failures were attributed before comparing to the active bytes.
incidents.what: A guard that could not be called independently had no negative protocol cases or positive controls. Regression failures were also misread, because macOS path aliases fail cwd-string assertions without any runtime location error.

incidents.title: A hygiene rule against conditional test omission needed a precise flagged and allowed set
incidents.rule: State both the flagged and the allowed set of a hygiene rule.
incidents.signature: A conditional skip or registration hides a test from the suite.
incidents.root_cause: No rule covered omission by condition.
incidents.what: Conditional omission through skipIf, runIf or registration inside a condition could hide tests. The ruling flags those and conditional registration at module or describe scope, and allows a conditional inside a test body and each tables.

incidents.title: An exit code 2 advisory wording in the gate runner defaulted to proceed
incidents.rule: Override permissive defaults on the release path.
incidents.signature: A gate returns an advisory status that a caller treats as pass.
incidents.root_cause: The runner default was proceed on an incomplete verdict.
incidents.what: The Foundry exit 2 advisory, proceed wording is the default that the final release card had to override.

incidents.title: A test checked only the dispatch argv of a child stage, not its semantics
incidents.rule: Test what a stage does, not how it was started.
incidents.signature: A stage is proven by what it was called with, not by what it did.
incidents.root_cause: The argv was easy to assert and the behavior was not.
incidents.what: A test covered the dispatch argv of a child stage and not the child stage behavior, and a database could survive into a later inventory owning stage.

incidents.title: A marker for an already activated revision used the pending path form
incidents.rule: Run the identity checker on the exact tree before committing any marker.
incidents.signature: A marker was committed without running the identity checker on the exact tree.
incidents.root_cause: The marker generator emitted the pending form regardless of whether the older copy was already active, and the checker was not run before the commit.
incidents.what: A lead marker for a revision whose older copy was already activated used the pending path form, and the identity checker reported a missing unlisted deletion on main until the edge was rewritten in the active path form.

incidents.title: A kill rehearsal met its timeout but nobody checked what the killed process left behind
incidents.rule: In a kill rehearsal, inspect the leftovers, and state the temporary directory setting the sweep depends on.
incidents.signature: A rehearsal passed on elapsed time while the leftovers of the killed run were unexamined.
incidents.root_cause: The rehearsal was judged on the timeout, and the temporary directory setting was not part of the operator contract.
incidents.what: In a kill rehearsal the timeout was easy to meet, but what the killed process leaves behind was the real question, and a registry sweep only reaps runs that used the same temporary directory setting.

incidents.title: A test fixture name collided with a framework built-in and only collection revealed it
incidents.rule: Run the framework list command on each new helper before its activation review.
incidents.signature: A helper looked fine in review and failed to load in every spec that imported it.
incidents.root_cause: The name was valid in isolation and nothing before collection compares it with the framework built-ins.
incidents.what: A QA browser helper registered an auto fixture named offline, which the Playwright version in use already registers as a built-in option, so every importing spec failed at collection.

incidents.title: A split-ownership root could not activate because identity had no registry support
incidents.rule: A root split by the registry needs registry-aware identity before its source row can activate.
incidents.signature: The identity checker rejected a root whose file had been reassigned to another row.
incidents.root_cause: Registry-aware identity was scheduled after the row that first needed it.
incidents.what: A root holding both a superseded suite and a path reassigned by the registry failed the partial activation check, because the registry half of the identity checker belonged to a later row.

incidents.title: A spec used import.meta under a package that loads specs as CommonJS
incidents.rule: Check the module form of the host package before using import.meta in a spec.
incidents.signature: A module-form feature worked in the author mind and would fail when the spec first loaded.
incidents.root_cause: The module form of the host package was not checked when the spec was written.
incidents.what: A pending spec computed its path with import.meta while the root package loads specs as CommonJS, so it would fail to load once activated.

incidents.title: A second reader of the same registry file was at risk of replacing the first
incidents.rule: One parser per shared file format, reviewed with a mutant and a malformed-input case.
incidents.signature: Two rows each needed to parse the same assignments file.
incidents.root_cause: Two rows owned overlapping parts of one file format.
incidents.what: The identity checker prep added a parser of the assignments file while a later row planned its own checks over the same file.

incidents.title: An activation was tied to an unreviewed successor and had to be re-ruled
incidents.rule: Do not tie the activation of a reviewed revision to an unreviewed successor.
incidents.signature: A shipped revision waited on a later revision that had not been reviewed.
incidents.root_cause: Activation timing was coupled to a successor whose review was still pending.
incidents.what: A ruling tied activation of a reviewed revision to the activation of its unreviewed successor; it was replaced so the reviewed revision activates in the first ready engineer row.

incidents.title: Landing a revision beside a supersession edge broke identity on main
incidents.rule: Run the identity checker after every landing, not only after markers; resolve supersession sources only among earlier revisions.
incidents.signature: The landing script passed while the identity checker was red on main.
incidents.root_cause: The checker picked supersession sources among all revisions, and the landing path never ran it.
incidents.what: Landing a QA revision beside an existing active-path supersession edge broke the identity checker, which resolved the edge source to the highest revision of any other root instead of the highest earlier one. The landing script did not run the checker, so main stayed red until a sweep caught it.

incidents.title: A chained amend reworded the previous commit after a failed revert
incidents.rule: Chain an amend only with && after a step whose success is checked, and confirm the HEAD subject before amending.
incidents.signature: A revert failed on an invalid flag and the next chained step changed the wrong commit.
incidents.root_cause: The amend was chained without checking that the revert succeeded.
incidents.what: A revert used an invalid flag and failed, and the chained amend then reworded the previous commit instead of the revert.

incidents.title: Acceptance ran bare vitest while the real gate ran setup then the FAST runner
incidents.rule: Acceptance must run the same commands preship runs, otherwise a green merge looks red or a red one looks green.
incidents.signature: A row merge looked red under the acceptance script and green under preship, or the reverse.
incidents.root_cause: The acceptance command was a shortcut that differed from the commands preship runs.
incidents.what: The lead acceptance script ran bare vitest, which stopped being valid once the server project gained a global setup that needs the per-stage database the FAST runner provides.

incidents.title: A reverted and re-landed QA revision got its marker approved at the wrong commit
incidents.rule: When a reverted revision is re-landed after an older copy became active, approve its marker at the re-land commit.
incidents.signature: The identity checker compared old active bytes at the approved commit.
incidents.root_cause: The approved commit named the original landing, not the re-land.
incidents.what: A QA revision reverted off main and re-landed later needed its marker approved at the re-land commit, because an older copy became active in between and the checker compares the old active bytes at the approved commit.

incidents.title: A shell variable followed by a colon and a letter became a history modifier
incidents.rule: In zsh, write the braces form of a variable before a colon.
incidents.signature: A shell string produced a truncated value without an error.
incidents.root_cause: The unbraced form is harmless in other shells and in most strings.
incidents.what: In zsh a variable followed by a colon and a letter is a history modifier (the :t tail), so the expanded string was silently changed.

incidents.title: A conditional omission could hide behind a helper, an alias or an early return
incidents.rule: Forbid conditional omission anywhere, with the same alias resolution as describe.
incidents.signature: A hygiene rule allowed omissions that took registrations out of a suite.
incidents.root_cause: The rule covered the direct describe shapes only.
incidents.what: A guarded registration inside a non-describe callback or helper, the suite alias of describe, and a conditional return in a describe body each omit registrations without being flagged by a narrower rule.

incidents.title: A revision marker added a second edge to bytes the previous marker already claimed
incidents.rule: Run the identity checker on a scratch clone before committing a marker, and take the edge from the newest pending earlier copy.
incidents.signature: The identity check went red with an old digest mismatch on a marker that looked complete.
incidents.root_cause: The marker author added an edge for the active bytes without noticing the earlier marker claimed them.
incidents.what: A marker for a new revision takes its edge from the newest pending earlier copy when one exists; an extra active-path edge to the same active bytes that the earlier marker already claims turned the identity check red.

incidents.title: Disjoint project discovery did not stop a suite from running twice
incidents.rule: A test that launches a runner must run it on a probe file, not the whole suite.
incidents.signature: One stage doubled its cases and its time.
incidents.root_cause: Disjoint discovery was assumed to imply disjoint execution.
incidents.what: A unit case launched the whole integration runner, so every integration case ran twice in the fast tier even though the projects were discovered disjointly.

incidents.title: A garbage collection test with a moved clock reaped the outer tier own live database
incidents.rule: A test that reaps shared resources must run before the outer run owns any.
incidents.signature: A test removed a database that belonged to the run that was executing it.
incidents.root_cause: The full tier created its database before running the harness step.
incidents.what: A garbage collection test with a moved clock could reap the live database of the outer tier running it.

incidents.title: A tracked file rewritten per tool mode could not stay clean in both tiers
incidents.rule: Do not track a file a tool rewrites per mode; generate it before the check that needs it.
incidents.signature: Two modes of one tool wrote different bytes to a tracked file.
incidents.root_cause: A generated file was tracked.
incidents.what: The development mode and the build mode of a framework write different bytes to the same tracked type declaration file, so neither tier could stay porcelain clean.

incidents.title: A generator default module augmentation made its committed output fail the type check
incidents.rule: Place generated type augmentation where the augmented module lives.
incidents.signature: Generated output failed to type check in the package where it landed.
incidents.root_cause: The augmentation referred to a module the package did not own.
incidents.what: A generator default module augmentation made its committed output fail the type check in the package where it landed.

incidents.title: A clean-tree gate failed on a fixture synthetic repo before the behavior under test
incidents.rule: A clean-tree gate applies to a fixture synthetic repo too.
incidents.signature: A test failed at the gate, not at the behavior it meant to exercise.
incidents.root_cause: The fixture was written as if the gate did not apply to it.
incidents.what: Generated launcher files in a fixture synthetic repo were not ignored before the fixture commit, so the clean-tree gate failed first.

incidents.title: A ruling widened a shared valid state and only some payloads followed
incidents.rule: When a ruling widens a shared valid state, change every payload that builds it.
incidents.signature: Some negatives passed against the tip only.
incidents.root_cause: Payloads were updated one at a time.
incidents.what: A ruling widened a shared valid state, and not every payload that builds the state was changed; negatives were proved only against the tip.

incidents.title: A count change was reconciled by totals and a route switch leaked into the default path
incidents.rule: Explain a count change by file identity, not by totals.
incidents.signature: Totals matched while the contents differed.
incidents.root_cause: Totals hide which files moved.
incidents.what: A count change was explained by totals, not by file identity, and a route-specific environment switch could leak into the default path.

incidents.title: A merge of main left an activation due and went red
incidents.rule: A merge of main carries every activation its new markers make due.
incidents.signature: The merge commit was red on its own.
incidents.root_cause: The merge was treated as plumbing.
incidents.what: A merge of main into a branch carrying another row activations did not carry every activation that main new markers made due.

incidents.title: A shape regex was used as ownership evidence for a sweep
incidents.rule: A sweep that decides by shape needs decoys.
incidents.signature: A sweep matched files it did not own.
incidents.root_cause: Shape is cheap to match and looks like ownership.
incidents.what: A sweep selected files by a shape regex and treated the match as ownership, with no decoys to prove it did not over-match.

incidents.title: Card text pointed at its own directory as the checkout
incidents.rule: Grep every card for the executable path; do not keep a duty beside the section that overrides it.
incidents.signature: Cards broke silently when the card set moved.
incidents.root_cause: The path was correct until the cards moved.
incidents.what: Card text pointed at its own directory as the checkout, and an override section sat beside the earlier duties it overrode.

incidents.title: A production build dirtied the tree and an example role was missing locally
incidents.rule: Check porcelain after every build; verify an example role exists locally.
incidents.signature: The tree was dirty after a successful build.
incidents.root_cause: The tracked generated file and the example role were never exercised locally.
incidents.what: A production build in a checkout that still tracks a per-mode generated file dirtied the tree, and an example env file named a role absent from the local cluster.

incidents.title: A chat pre-approval did not lift an explicit approval rule
incidents.rule: When an approval prompt expires, queue and report; never rephrase around the rule.
incidents.signature: An upload stalled on an approval prompt that expired.
incidents.root_cause: The pre-approval was assumed to carry over.
incidents.what: An explicit tool approval rule still prompted after a chat pre-approval, and the prompt expired while the operator was away.

incidents.title: A readiness check ran without the dispatcher environment
incidents.rule: Run readiness checks with the live dispatcher environment.
incidents.signature: A missing variable read as a missing tool.
incidents.root_cause: The operator shell differs from the dispatcher environment.
incidents.what: A readiness check ran in the operator shell without the agent and database variables the live dispatcher has.

incidents.title: A package launcher in an uninstalled source clone reached for the registry
incidents.rule: Install offline before running a package launcher in a source clone.
incidents.signature: A dispatch hung or failed on a network lookup.
incidents.root_cause: The launcher resolves the package before running it.
incidents.what: A package launcher run in an uninstalled source clone reached for the registry before it dispatched the script.

incidents.title: A marker generator covered every payload of a root when only part was approved
incidents.rule: A marker covers only what the ruling approved.
incidents.signature: A marker claimed more than the ruling approved.
incidents.root_cause: The generator knew roots, not approvals.
incidents.what: A marker generator emitted an edge for every payload of a root, giving four edges where the ruling approved two.

incidents.title: Sibling fixture factories lacked the metadata that makes a checker required
incidents.rule: Sibling fixture factories carry the same required metadata.
incidents.signature: A positive control passed without reaching its negative.
incidents.root_cause: Each factory was written alone.
incidents.what: Complete metadata absence tells a required checker from an optional path, and sibling fixture factories did not carry the same required metadata, so the controls never reached the negatives they claim to test.

incidents.title: A docs-only row was accepted by judgment instead of one mechanical diff
incidents.rule: Accept a docs-only row by one name-status diff against the stated parent.
incidents.signature: Acceptance depended on reading.
incidents.root_cause: Scope was checked by reading, not by a diff.
incidents.what: A docs-only rehearsal row needs a mechanical acceptance: one name-status diff against the stated parent proves file scope, plus the one state cell and no cited commit id.

incidents.title: Rename detection reported a false rename in a merge
incidents.rule: Do not accept either side of a reported rename; confirm the blob against main.
incidents.signature: A merge showed a rename and delete that did not happen.
incidents.root_cause: Similarity is not identity.
incidents.what: When two branches both activated the same pending root, rename detection paired the deleted pending copy with the near-identical new revision copy.

incidents.title: A per-root checker summary undercounted edges
incidents.rule: Derive the marker set from the manifests, not from a per-root summary.
incidents.signature: The summary showed fewer edges than the manifests hold.
incidents.root_cause: The summary groups by root, so shared edges collapse.
incidents.what: The per-root summary of the identity checker undercounts edges.

incidents.title: A slow stage was trimmed by cases instead of cut by grouping files
incidents.rule: Group files that parallelize cleanly; do not trim cases whose timeouts are fixed.
incidents.signature: A stage kept growing while case trimming saved little.
incidents.root_cause: Trimming was aimed at cases that could not move.
incidents.what: A stage that grows by whole files of process-spawning cases free of database use is cut by grouping the files; the slow cases in older files were fixed timeouts written into protected bytes or plan rules.

incidents.title: An override changed the lockfile and an offline clone could not install it
incidents.rule: Warm override metadata with a frozen install in a scratch clone before any offline install
incidents.signature: An offline install failed for lack of supply-chain metadata.
incidents.root_cause: An override changed the lockfile, and its supply-chain metadata had never been fetched online, so an offline clone could not install it.
incidents.what: An override changed the lockfile, and its supply-chain metadata had never been fetched online, so an offline clone could not install it.

incidents.title: An override was written without reading the dependent declared range
incidents.rule: Read the dependent declared range in the registry before writing an override; an out of range override needs a direct probe of the code path
incidents.signature: An override landed outside the range the dependent declares.
incidents.root_cause: An override was written before the dependent declared range was read; an exact pin or a caret major puts the override outside it, and no one probed the code path.
incidents.what: An override was written before the dependent declared range was read; an exact pin or a caret major puts the override outside it, and no one probed the code path.

incidents.title: FAST stayed green while a command-adapter fixture missed a new execution project
incidents.rule: Update every command-adapter fixture when an execution project is added, and do not trust FAST alone
incidents.signature: Only the FULL path caught the missing project.
incidents.root_cause: A new execution project was added and not every command-adapter fixture recognized it; the fast tier does not exercise that fixture.
incidents.what: A new execution project was added and not every command-adapter fixture recognized it; the fast tier does not exercise that fixture.

incidents.title: A one-parser requirement was pinned by only one kind of test
incidents.rule: Pin a one-parser requirement both structurally and behaviorally
incidents.signature: A second parser could appear without failing a test.
incidents.root_cause: A one-parser requirement was pinned structurally or behaviorally, not both, so a second parser could either hide in another file or diverge on an input no test used.
incidents.what: A one-parser requirement was pinned structurally or behaviorally, not both, so a second parser could either hide in another file or diverge on an input no test used.

incidents.title: A rehearsal mixed automatic guards with procedural stops
incidents.rule: Separate automatic guards from procedural stops in a rehearsal, and plant the state change relative to the actual baseline
incidents.signature: The rehearsal could not say which guard fired.
incidents.root_cause: A negative-case rehearsal mixed automatic guards with procedural stops, and the planted state change was not set relative to the actual baseline.
incidents.what: A negative-case rehearsal mixed automatic guards with procedural stops, and the planted state change was not set relative to the actual baseline.

incidents.title: A negative grep was taken as proof that a removal ruling was complete
incidents.rule: Check each named duty and its follow-through lines; a negative grep alone proves nothing
incidents.signature: The forbidden token was gone and the duty remained.
incidents.root_cause: A grep found no forbidden token left and was read as proof that a removal ruling was complete, while named duties and their follow-through lines remained.
incidents.what: A grep found no forbidden token left and was read as proof that a removal ruling was complete, while named duties and their follow-through lines remained.

incidents.title: A citation check by search alone could miss a changed fact
incidents.rule: Compare cited ranges by diff when a version bump moves pinned-source citations
incidents.signature: A moved range was matched by text while its behavior changed.
incidents.root_cause: A version bump moved pinned-source citations, and a search finds the text but cannot show whether the text around it changed.
incidents.what: A version bump moved pinned-source citations, and a search finds the text but cannot show whether the text around it changed.

incidents.title: A single stage time on a loaded host was read as a measurement
incidents.rule: Decide timing rules on repeated runs with the load recorded, never on one stage time
incidents.signature: The same tree read 30.5 s and then 14.9 s.
incidents.root_cause: One stage time on a loaded host was treated as a measurement; the same tree gave 30.5 s in one run and 14.9 s in the next.
incidents.what: One stage time on a loaded host was treated as a measurement; the same tree gave 30.5 s in one run and 14.9 s in the next.

incidents.title: An allowlist fix turned gate tests green while the runner skipped the new project
incidents.rule: Prove a new project ran by its own marker, not only by the shared stage record
incidents.signature: The gate tests passed and the new project never ran.
incidents.root_cause: An adapter allowlist fix made the gate tests green while the delegated runner silently skipped the new project; only the shared stage record was checked.
incidents.what: An adapter allowlist fix made the gate tests green while the delegated runner silently skipped the new project; only the shared stage record was checked.

incidents.title: A typecheck failed in a shared helper the revision did not own
incidents.rule: Fix a shared helper in its own row, never inside the consumer root
incidents.signature: The red was in code the revision could not touch.
incidents.root_cause: A typecheck over pending destinations failed in a shared active helper the revision does not own, which invited an edit or a suppression in the consumer root.
incidents.what: A typecheck over pending destinations failed in a shared active helper the revision does not own, which invited an edit or a suppression in the consumer root.

incidents.title: A ledger derived from a token range went stale when a row joined the range
incidents.rule: Regenerate a ledger derived from a range at each revision and state the derived count
incidents.signature: The ledger no longer matched the plan.
incidents.root_cause: A staging ledger derived from a token range went stale whenever a row joined that range.
incidents.what: A staging ledger derived from a token range went stale whenever a row joined that range.

incidents.title: An inline directive could bypass a lint rule on a protected path
incidents.rule: Scope noInlineConfig by files; an ignored directive still prints a warning
incidents.signature: A bypass could be written inline.
incidents.root_cause: Inline directives could switch off a rule on a protected path; a files-scoped noInlineConfig disables them for that path only and the ignored directive still warns.
incidents.what: Inline directives could switch off a rule on a protected path; a files-scoped noInlineConfig disables them for that path only and the ignored directive still warns.

incidents.title: A sandbox permission failure was at risk of reading as a code defect
incidents.rule: Treat a permission-denied run as missing evidence and rerun it where it is permitted
incidents.signature: The red had nothing to do with the code.
incidents.root_cause: A review fast run failed because the sandbox denied nested process listing, which looks like a code failure.
incidents.what: A review fast run failed because the sandbox denied nested process listing, which looks like a code failure.

incidents.title: Two review titles named the wrong reviewer
incidents.rule: Check the attribution line of every report before landing it
incidents.signature: The report carried another reviewer name.
incidents.root_cause: Reviewers reused a template and left the previous reviewer name in the title, so two reports were attributed to the wrong reviewer.
incidents.what: Reviewers reused a template and left the previous reviewer name in the title, so two reports were attributed to the wrong reviewer.

incidents.title: One adapter rejection looked like ten separate defects
incidents.rule: Before triaging many reds, read the child output to find the one shared cause
incidents.signature: Ten failures shared one cause.
incidents.root_cause: An adapter rejection at the first FULL phase fanned out into intended-fault failures and smoke-wait poll timeouts that looked like separate defects.
incidents.what: An adapter rejection at the first FULL phase fanned out into intended-fault failures and smoke-wait poll timeouts that looked like separate defects.

incidents.title: A setup failure was at risk of counting as a test run
incidents.rule: Do not count a setup-only failure as a run
incidents.signature: The run failed before any test started.
incidents.root_cause: Setup-only failures of a clean-clone run, such as a missing package-manager cache or a missing metadata cache in a moved private environment, are not test executions but could be counted as runs.
incidents.what: Setup-only failures of a clean-clone run, such as a missing package-manager cache or a missing metadata cache in a moved private environment, are not test executions but could be counted as runs.

incidents.title: A precommit check reported a merge-brought approval as unreachable
incidents.rule: Judge reachability on the committed merge, not on the precommit state
incidents.signature: The check read the wrong commit.
incidents.root_cause: A precommit identity check that reads HEAD reported a merge-brought approval as unreachable during the merge.
incidents.what: A precommit identity check that reads HEAD reported a merge-brought approval as unreachable during the merge.

incidents.title: A runtime value was at risk of being invented to quiet the compiler
incidents.rule: Copy the typed input and delete from the copy; never fabricate a runtime value to quiet the compiler
incidents.signature: The compiler asked for a value the code should not have.
incidents.root_cause: An ambient type augmentation made a field required, and the easy fix was to fabricate a runtime value such as NODE_ENV.
incidents.what: An ambient type augmentation made a field required, and the easy fix was to fabricate a runtime value such as NODE_ENV.

incidents.title: A guessed commit id was sent to two teammates
incidents.rule: Never cite a commit id in a message before git has printed it
incidents.signature: Two teammates received a wrong id.
incidents.root_cause: A guessed commit id for a landing was sent to two teammates, who then needed corrections.
incidents.what: A guessed commit id for a landing was sent to two teammates, who then needed corrections.

incidents.title: Three sends failed because a packed string went out as one argument
incidents.rule: Check the exit status of every send, and pass real arguments, not a packed string
incidents.signature: The sends failed with exit 1.
incidents.root_cause: In zsh an unquoted variable does not word split, so a loop that does set -- on a packed string sent the whole string as one argument.
incidents.what: In zsh an unquoted variable does not word split, so a loop that does set -- on a packed string sent the whole string as one argument.

incidents.title: Two rows were green alone and red together
incidents.rule: Rehearse the merged stack, not the branches
incidents.signature: The combination failed and neither branch did.
incidents.root_cause: A scoped lint rule from one row and a generated file with a disable banner from another were red only in combination.
incidents.what: A scoped lint rule from one row and a generated file with a disable banner from another were red only in combination.

incidents.title: A FULL step deadline was shorter than the measured stage time
incidents.rule: Recheck FULL step budgets against measured FAST stage times whenever the suite grows
incidents.signature: The deadline sat below the measured time.
incidents.root_cause: The FULL unit deadline was 90 s while unit took 93 to 103 s in FAST.
incidents.what: The FULL unit deadline was 90 s while unit took 93 to 103 s in FAST.

incidents.title: A slow suite was a candidate for cutting before it was profiled
incidents.rule: Profile before cutting tests
incidents.signature: The slow part was not where cuts would land.
incidents.root_cause: Parallel test files and one batched object read gave back about 90 s without touching a QA byte; the unprofiled tree was red on a loaded host.
incidents.what: Parallel test files and one batched object read gave back about 90 s without touching a QA byte; the unprofiled tree was red on a loaded host.

incidents.title: A regex literal was read as a file path by the permission checker
incidents.rule: Put probe code in a file inside the scratch tree; prefer plain string tests over regex literals on a command line
incidents.signature: A harmless probe was blocked as a path access.
incidents.root_cause: A permission checker read a slash delimited regular expression literal on a command line as a file path.
incidents.what: A permission checker read a slash delimited regular expression literal on a command line as a file path.

incidents.title: A relative path was resolved against the wrong root
incidents.rule: Use absolute paths when working across worktrees
incidents.signature: The command was refused for a path it did not name.
incidents.root_cause: A relative path that climbs into a sibling worktree was resolved by the permission checker against the workspace root and landed outside it.
incidents.what: A relative path that climbs into a sibling worktree was resolved by the permission checker against the workspace root and landed outside it.

incidents.title: A network-denied dependency audit was neither a finding nor a pass
incidents.rule: Classify a network-denied audit by its exact signature, and keep other errors with the same code failing
incidents.signature: The audit could not run and exited like a result.
incidents.root_cause: A network-denied dependency audit is neither a vulnerability finding nor a pass, and an error code shared with other failures hides the difference.
incidents.what: A network-denied dependency audit is neither a vulnerability finding nor a pass, and an error code shared with other failures hides the difference.

incidents.title: A helper was fixed and a caller still passed a literal empty object
incidents.rule: Check every caller of a fixed helper with a strict destination compile
incidents.signature: The helper fix left a caller broken.
incidents.root_cause: Fixing a shared helper internals did not fix a caller that passes a literal empty object to its typed parameter.
incidents.what: Fixing a shared helper internals did not fix a caller that passes a literal empty object to its typed parameter.

incidents.title: A commit skipped the machine-wide pre-commit scanner
incidents.rule: Never override the hook path; if it happens, amend with hooks on right away
incidents.signature: The scanner never ran.
incidents.root_cause: A commit was made with the hook path overridden, which skipped a machine-wide pre-commit scanner.
incidents.what: A commit was made with the hook path overridden, which skipped a machine-wide pre-commit scanner.

incidents.title: A scratch swap of revision bytes failed the identity gate as designed
incidents.rule: Use the real approved chain in a causal proof, not just the bytes
incidents.signature: The gate failed for the right reason, which the proof had not intended.
incidents.root_cause: A scratch swap of revision bytes without their approved supersession chain correctly fails the identity gate.
incidents.what: A scratch swap of revision bytes without their approved supersession chain correctly fails the identity gate.

incidents.title: A fixed test count in an exit criterion went stale
incidents.rule: State an exit as the full active inventory with zero failed or skipped, name the qualifying-run rule, and disclose excluded runs
incidents.signature: The count no longer matched the suite.
incidents.root_cause: A fixed test count written into an exit criterion goes stale as the suite moves.
incidents.what: A fixed test count written into an exit criterion goes stale as the suite moves.

incidents.title: Two loaded-host reds shared one cause and were at risk of a timeout bump
incidents.rule: When reds share a cause class that a pending row removes, carry the acceptance to that row, not a timeout or a retry
incidents.signature: The cheap fix hid the shared cause.
incidents.root_cause: Two loaded-host reds shared one cause class that a pending row removes, and raising a timeout or retrying a case would hide it.
incidents.what: Two loaded-host reds shared one cause class that a pending row removes, and raising a timeout or retrying a case would hide it.

incidents.title: A shared host reached load 491 and unrelated deadlines failed
incidents.rule: Cap concurrent heavy runs across the team and record load at start and end
incidents.signature: Unrelated deadlines failed under a shared load.
incidents.root_cause: The cap on heavy runs was per worker, so the team total overloaded the host to a load of 491.
incidents.what: The cap on heavy runs was per worker, so the team total overloaded the host to a load of 491.

incidents.title: A reviewer proposed text was at risk of being applied by its own author
incidents.rule: Apply a reviewer exact text through a third party, with digested backups, a proposer re-review and a separate re-check
incidents.signature: The author could soften the reviewer text.
incidents.root_cause: A reviewer exact proposed text was applied by someone with no independent check, with no backup of the pre-edit set.
incidents.what: A reviewer exact proposed text was applied by someone with no independent check, with no backup of the pre-edit set.

incidents.title: A performance refactor was checked only on the real tree
incidents.rule: Prove a performance refactor with old and new on the same failure fixtures
incidents.signature: Equal output on the real tree hid changed failure behavior.
incidents.root_cause: A performance refactor of a checker was at risk of being accepted on equal output on the real tree alone.
incidents.what: A performance refactor of a checker was at risk of being accepted on equal output on the real tree alone.

incidents.title: A clean-tree positive did not exercise the working-file context
incidents.rule: Plant a harmless byte difference before proving a refusal when the baseline is chosen by byte equality
incidents.signature: The clean tree matched the baseline, so the refusal path never ran.
incidents.root_cause: A clean-tree positive did not test the working-file context of a checker that picks its baseline by byte equality.
incidents.what: A clean-tree positive did not test the working-file context of a checker that picks its baseline by byte equality.

incidents.title: An empty environment caller was at risk of being repaired with inherited values
incidents.rule: Prove the input is empty and that the refusal fails without its guard
incidents.signature: The inherited values hid the empty case.
incidents.root_cause: An empty environment caller can be repaired by passing inherited values, and the test then no longer proves the empty case.
incidents.what: An empty environment caller can be repaired by passing inherited values, and the test then no longer proves the empty case.

incidents.title: A classifier kept a legacy pattern list beside a new exact signature
incidents.rule: Probe a classifier extension with lookalike negatives
incidents.signature: The legacy list still matched lookalikes.
incidents.root_cause: A classifier kept a legacy pattern list while adding an exact signature, which extends rather than narrows what it accepts.
incidents.what: A classifier kept a legacy pattern list while adding an exact signature, which extends rather than narrows what it accepts.

incidents.title: A fix was named for one card while four siblings carried the same command
incidents.rule: When applying a fix, search for siblings of the named instance and report them
incidents.signature: The siblings were left unfixed or silently changed.
incidents.root_cause: A reviewer named one instance of a rule while four sibling cards carry the same command.
incidents.what: A reviewer named one instance of a rule while four sibling cards carry the same command.

incidents.title: A hand-made merge could differ from the mechanical merge unnoticed
incidents.rule: Verify a hand-made merge against a mechanical merge of the same parents
incidents.signature: The extra changes sat inside a large merge.
incidents.root_cause: A hand-made merge was not compared with a mechanical merge of the same parents.
incidents.what: A hand-made merge was not compared with a mechanical merge of the same parents.

incidents.title: A retry wrapper logged the dependency stderr privately and starved the caller diagnosis
incidents.rule: A wrapper must preserve the failure channel of what it wraps, passing the last cause through on final failure.
incidents.signature: A long outage was reported with an empty cause.
incidents.root_cause: A wrapper around a flaky credential helper captured the helper stderr into its own log and emitted nothing on its own stderr, so a classifier above it saw an empty stderr and reported no category for a 13 hour outage.
incidents.what: A wrapper around a flaky credential helper captured the helper stderr into its own log and emitted nothing on its own stderr, so a classifier above it saw an empty stderr and reported no category for a 13 hour outage.

incidents.title: A digest manifest without digests was cited as evidence
incidents.rule: Check that a manifest has one digest per line before citing it
incidents.signature: The manifest looked complete and held no digests.
incidents.root_cause: A backup digest manifest listed file names with no digests and was cited as evidence.
incidents.what: A backup digest manifest listed file names with no digests and was cited as evidence.

incidents.title: A commit swept another session uncommitted entries
incidents.rule: In a shared checkout, stage only your own paths and check the log for foreign commits before writing
incidents.signature: Entries landed under a message about a different lesson.
incidents.root_cause: Another session committed in a shared checkout and swept a teammate uncommitted entries into its own commit.
incidents.what: Another session committed in a shared checkout and swept a teammate uncommitted entries into its own commit.

incidents.title: A split of the dominant test file saved about zero
incidents.rule: Profile a dominant file and check shared inventory assertions and the critical path before splitting it
incidents.signature: The split was on the shorter branch of the critical path.
incidents.root_cause: A dominant test file was assumed parallelizable, but splitting it in the shorter concurrent branch saves about zero.
incidents.what: A dominant test file was assumed parallelizable, but splitting it in the shorter concurrent branch saves about zero.

incidents.title: A measurement was at risk of coming from an overlay in a scratch tree
incidents.rule: Measure on the exact tree that carries the file and label every figure with its SHA
incidents.signature: The figures had no tree behind them.
incidents.root_cause: The assigned base lacked a file the measurer was asked to measure, which invited overlaying bytes into a scratch tree.
incidents.what: The assigned base lacked a file the measurer was asked to measure, which invited overlaying bytes into a scratch tree.

incidents.title: A prompt render succeeded without reading the card bodies
incidents.rule: Verify external card bytes separately from a successful prompt render
incidents.signature: The render referenced the cards by path only.
incidents.root_cause: A successful prompt render was taken as evidence of card content, but it referenced the cards by path without reading their bodies.
incidents.what: A successful prompt render was taken as evidence of card content, but it referenced the cards by path without reading their bodies.

incidents.title: Approval of role cards in prose was at risk of standing in for a runtime check
incidents.rule: Run the planted-dispute rehearsal and the incomplete-verdict dry run at the exit commit; prose approval is not runtime evidence
incidents.signature: No run backed the approval.
incidents.root_cause: Prose approval of role cards is not runtime evidence of how they behave.
incidents.what: Prose approval of role cards is not runtime evidence of how they behave.

incidents.title: A ledger review that started from the author list could inherit its gaps
incidents.rule: Derive a ledger from the plan yourself before reading the author list, then compare
incidents.signature: The reviewer saw only what the author listed.
incidents.root_cause: A ledger was checked by reading the author list first, which carries the author omissions into the review.
incidents.what: A ledger was checked by reading the author list first, which carries the author omissions into the review.

incidents.title: A revision review could re-read an unchanged downstream table
incidents.rule: Diff the downstream table first when a revision only adds upstream rows
incidents.signature: The unchanged part cost review time and hid the real delta.
incidents.root_cause: A plan revision only added upstream rows, and the downstream table was byte identical.
incidents.what: A plan revision only added upstream rows, and the downstream table was byte identical.

incidents.title: A BLOCKED result came from a deadline before the plant ran
incidents.rule: A negative proof counts only with a passing control, the plant own execution marker and the named failed step
incidents.signature: The negative never reached the plant.
incidents.root_cause: Earlier BLOCKED attempts stopped at a loaded-host deadline before the plant ran, so the block was not caused by the plant.
incidents.what: Earlier BLOCKED attempts stopped at a loaded-host deadline before the plant ran, so the block was not caused by the plant.

incidents.title: A team runtime cap blocked new teammates behind retained idle ones
incidents.rule: Release then close the longest idle teammate to free a slot; prefer larger batches over more teammates
incidents.signature: The cap was reached with idle teammates that could not be closed.
incidents.root_cause: A team runtime caps active teammates at ten, and a retained teammate cannot be closed until it is released.
incidents.what: A team runtime caps active teammates at ten, and a retained teammate cannot be closed until it is released.

incidents.title: A leak scanner matched part of a generated name and blocked uploads
incidents.rule: Scan the whole tree after every merge, and fix a scanner false match with an encoded safe prefix proved by planted cases
incidents.signature: The scan failed closed on a merge long after the files were added.
incidents.root_cause: A leak scanner word list matched part of a time zone name in generated framework types, and the push range scan never covered those files until a merge.
incidents.what: A leak scanner word list matched part of a time zone name in generated framework types, and the push range scan never covered those files until a merge.

incidents.title: A hold outcome had no proof that nothing changed
incidents.rule: Prove a hold by the remote main SHA unchanged before and after and an empty porcelain on the build clone
incidents.signature: No change looks the same as no run.
incidents.root_cause: A hold index is an explicit no-selection outcome and needed proof that nothing moved.
incidents.what: A hold index is an explicit no-selection outcome and needed proof that nothing moved.

incidents.title: An auto-merge of a helper could lose an activation or coverage unnoticed
incidents.rule: Prove an auto-merge by an ordered two-parent history check and an exact-run project inventory
incidents.signature: The bytes were right and a project could still drop out.
incidents.root_cause: Approved successor bytes plus an explicit predecessor edge make a helper auto-merge safe, but do not show that no activation or coverage was lost.
incidents.what: Approved successor bytes plus an explicit predecessor edge make a helper auto-merge safe, but do not show that no activation or coverage was lost.

incidents.title: Automated tests passed while nobody had walked the real site
incidents.rule: Walk the real site after each milestone and feature close, and write each defect as a failing test first
incidents.signature: The suite covered what was written, not what a person would click.
incidents.root_cause: Nobody walked the real site after a milestone, so defects in the real flow were not covered by any test.
incidents.what: Nobody walked the real site after a milestone, so defects in the real flow were not covered by any test.

incidents.title: Four of five test authors stopped at the same undeclared seam
incidents.rule: Audit a proposed test by the seam it declares, and checkpoint per root rather than per batch
incidents.signature: Authors stopped at the same boundary.
incidents.root_cause: A tier audit judged proposed unit cases by behavior instead of by declared seam, so four of five authors stopped at the same boundary.
incidents.what: A tier audit judged proposed unit cases by behavior instead of by declared seam, so four of five authors stopped at the same boundary.

incidents.title: A proposed subject was treated as if its seam were declared
incidents.rule: Declare the import seam; ownership or authorization of a subject does not declare a callable boundary
incidents.signature: The missing binding was not declared anywhere.
incidents.root_cause: Authorizing a synthetic collection or owning a generated field was read as declaring an importable, callable boundary.
incidents.what: Authorizing a synthetic collection or owning a generated field was read as declaring an importable, callable boundary.

incidents.title: A correct not-found page was served with a 200 status
incidents.rule: Assert the response status and the rendered body together
incidents.signature: The page looked right and the status was wrong.
