incidents.root_cause: A not-found page rendered correctly while the response status was 200, and no test checked both.
incidents.what: A not-found page rendered correctly while the response status was 200, and no test checked both.

incidents.title: A third-party avatar request was made without anyone noticing
incidents.rule: Assert that a page makes no request to a third-party origin unless declared
incidents.signature: The page looked right and still contacted a third party.
incidents.root_cause: A third-party avatar request left the site while the page looked correct and no test watched outbound requests.
incidents.what: A third-party avatar request left the site while the page looked correct and no test watched outbound requests.

incidents.title: A short password check created the one-time account instead of showing an error
incidents.rule: Run destructive checks on a one-time form last, and use a repeatable form for validation checks
incidents.signature: The probe succeeded and consumed the one-time form.
incidents.root_cause: The create-first-user form has no minimum password length, so a short password check created the account.
incidents.what: The create-first-user form has no minimum password length, so a short password check created the account.

incidents.title: Ancestry was at risk of standing in for a clean tree or a checker run
incidents.rule: Do not use ancestry as evidence of a clean tree, a checker run or bracketing observations

incidents.title: Bare angle-bracket slots turned a Markdown note into raw text after structural checks passed
incidents.rule: Verify Markdown by the target renderer's own parse, not by structural lint; never leave a bare <slot> outside code.
incidents.signature: The note passed every structural check and still showed raw text after the first slot.
incidents.root_cause: Formatting was judged by structural lint (balanced fences, headings present) instead of by the target renderer's own parse. The renderer's inline-HTML start rule and bare-URL rule were never modelled, so an unclosed element passed every check.
incidents.what: An agent wrote Markdown study notes with angle-bracket slots such as <validation>, <contract test> and <one reason> in prose, and a generic type such as Stream<Student> in a quote. A Markdown note app's live editor opens an inline HTML element on a less-than sign followed by a letter-word. No slot was ever closed, so the editor stayed in HTML mode and every later line (headings, lists, tables, diagram code fences) showed as raw text to the end of the note. Measured with the app's own tokenizer: 674 of 700 lines showed as raw text, and only 0 of 4 diagrams and 3 of 74 headings rendered. The reading view silently deleted the slot words. The agent had earlier said the formatting was fine, based on balanced fences and present headings. Only the user seeing the broken note caught it. A second trap turned up in the fix: a backslash escape right after a bare URL does not escape, because the editor's bare-URL token swallows the backslash. Backticks work.

incidents.what: a checker fix was revised in place from revision 2 to revision 3; the rechecker was asked to show the new tests fail on the revision 2 bytes, but those bytes (size and digest recorded in a review) existed nowhere: not in any worktree, temporary folder or the repository object store, so the red witness had to fall back to the pre-fix original plus a historical review

incidents.title: Time stamps written from an estimate ran ahead of the clock
incidents.rule: Read the clock immediately before writing any time stamp; when you did not, write a bounded range from the last real reads, never an estimate
incidents.signature: Four rulings were labelled 19:35 to 19:50 while the clock read 19:26 at the next check.
incidents.root_cause: time stamps were estimated instead of read, and estimates drift ahead in fast work
incidents.what: during a burst of rulings the lead labelled four of them 19:35 to 19:50 by estimate; the clock read at the next check said 19:26, and an earlier label was nine minutes ahead too

incidents.title: A physical copy of a shared package store carried its registry of outside links
incidents.rule: Before copying a shared tool cache into an isolated run, list its links; a registry of outside links is metadata to exclude, while any other outside link is a containment failure
incidents.signature: A preparation check that no copied link resolves outside the copy stopped the first authorized run before setup.
incidents.root_cause: the copy included the store's projects registry, which is metadata made of links to every project that ever used the store, so the containment check read it as a breach
incidents.what: a reviewed acceptance recipe copied the shared package store into a private home and verified that no copied link resolves outside the copy; the store's projects registry held 373 links to every project that ever used the store (temporary clones, worktrees, fixtures), 353 already dangling, so the first authorized run stopped in preparation before setup and nothing ran

incidents.title: A size limit on each transported record and a full-identity requirement were specified together with no framing
incidents.rule: When a transport limit and a completeness requirement meet, specify the framing and reconstruction, and test with long and non-ASCII identities
incidents.signature: A timing spec required every record to fit 512 bytes and to carry full file and case identity, and a long path could not satisfy both.
incidents.root_cause: two requirements in the spec could not both hold for long identities, and the spec did not say how an oversized record is represented
incidents.what: a timing spec required every record to fit 512 bytes (the portable atomic pipe write) and also to carry the full file path and test name; a long path or title cannot satisfy both, and the spec gave no representation for an oversized record, so the implementer could only truncate, hash or drop

incidents.title: An authorization point was placed after the first event that needs the identity
incidents.rule: Put the authorization point before the first event that must carry the identity, and test the forged-object negative
incidents.signature: A spec required records emitted early in a run to carry an identifier that was not created until later in the run.
incidents.root_cause: the authorization point was placed later in the run than the first event that must carry the identity
incidents.what: a spec switched on timing collection at the point where the test database was allocated, but also required the earlier test selection and discovery records to carry the inner run identifier, which stayed private to the harness until that point

incidents.title: Gating by an environment variable leaked into nested runners that copy the environment
incidents.rule: Never treat an inherited environment variable as authority; bind it to the process that was authorized
incidents.signature: A spec claimed an opt-in feature was inert in nested child runs, but a nested helper copied the whole environment and started a fresh runner directly.
incidents.root_cause: authority was carried by an inherited environment variable, and a child that copies the environment inherits the authority with it
incidents.what: a spec claimed detailed timing was inert in nested child runs, but a nested test helper copies the whole environment and launches a fresh runner directly, bypassing the entry point that would have stripped the enabling switches

incidents.title: Per-item sequential timeouts could not meet a global deadline stated in the spec
incidents.rule: When a spec sets a global bound, check the existing per-item loop arithmetic; sequential waits add up
incidents.signature: A spec required every process group to be reaped within 10 s, while the shutdown code waited on the groups one after another at about 10 s each.
incidents.root_cause: a global bound was written without checking the arithmetic of the existing per-item loop, where sequential waits add up
incidents.what: a spec required all process groups and their descendants to be reaped within 10 s of the first failure, while the harness stops the groups one after another, allowing about 5 s to terminate and 5 s to reap each

incidents.title: A reviewed recipe never ran its real tool queries because every control stubbed them
incidents.rule: A stubbed control proves the recipe's logic, not its commands; before an authorized run, execute every real read-only command once against the pinned tool versions
incidents.signature: A recipe passed its dry run, control run and copy cases, then its first real run stopped in preparation on an unsupported option.
incidents.root_cause: every control replaced the real tool calls with stubs, so the commands themselves were never executed against the pinned tool version before the authorized run
incidents.what: an acceptance recipe passed its dry run, its control run, six exit controls and 26 copy cases, all with stubbed package manager calls; the first real authorized run stopped in preparation because one query passed an option the pinned manager version does not support ("Unknown option"), so a scheduled run was lost before setup

incidents.title: A landing helper piped a guarded commit into a formatter, so the guard's failure did not stop the cleanup
incidents.rule: Never pipe a gating command into a formatter in a chain whose later steps destroy the input; check the gate's own exit status
incidents.signature: A scrub guard failed, yet the helper went on to delete the source file because the pipeline reported the formatter's zero status.
incidents.root_cause: the guarded step was piped into a formatter, so the chain saw the formatter's exit status and the guard's failure could not stop the later destructive step
incidents.what: a shell helper ran a copy, then a scrub-and-commit script piped into "tail -1", then a cleanup that deletes the source file from the author's worktree; the scrub failed on two absolute paths, but the pipeline's status was the formatter's (zero), so the cleanup ran and the only copy left was an uncommitted file in the main checkout; nothing was lost because the operator noticed

incidents.title: A restated rule gained a qualifier the original ruling never had
incidents.rule: When a ruling is restated in a spec, copy its population word for word; a qualifier borrowed from another purpose narrows an alarm, so diff every restated condition against the ruling's own words and fix each sibling copy
incidents.signature: A ruling said to report every sample over a limit at once, but the spec that restated it said to report only eligible samples.
incidents.root_cause: the restatement borrowed a qualifier from a different purpose (which samples count toward calibration) and applied it to an alarm, and the same wording was copied into a sibling document
incidents.what: a ruling required that any sample over a time limit be reported to the lead at once. A spec author restated it in a precondition document and in a companion spec as "an eligible sample over the limit". A sample made ineligible by load or transport loss could still exceed the limit, and under the restated text it would be kept for later instead of reported. An earlier review had already asked that the rule not be narrowed to eligible attempts

incidents.title: A stored admission record left out the tool versions it was produced under
incidents.rule: A stored proof that unlocks a faster or riskier route must carry the tool versions it was produced under and compare them at use; a mismatch or a missing field takes the safe route with a named reason, never the fast one
incidents.signature: A per-file audit that admits concurrent test runs recorded no tool versions, so a proof from one toolchain would unlock the fast route under another.
incidents.root_cause: the register was keyed on the file and its content but not on the toolchain whose behavior the proof depended on
incidents.what: a test harness kept an audit register that decided, per test file, whether files could safely run concurrently. The register recorded no interpreter or package manager version. An entry proven under one toolchain would still admit concurrency under another, and a missing or malformed version had no defined outcome

incidents.title: Ownership registered before a create made a definite duplicate error drop a foreign database
incidents.rule: Ownership recorded before a create covers an uncertain outcome only; on a definite already-exists error release the claim before rethrowing, and test with a pre-existing object under the exact name
incidents.signature: A harness queued a drop of its test database before creating it, so a create that failed because the name existed would drop a database it never made.
incidents.root_cause: ownership was claimed before the create outcome was known and was never released when the outcome turned out to be a definite duplicate
incidents.what: a test harness queued the drop of a test database before issuing the create, on purpose, so that an uncertain create outcome would still be cleaned up. A create that failed with a definite already-exists error would then drop a database this run never created. A helper in the test suite recorded ownership the same way. Random name suffixes made a real collision improbable, so this was an ownership-rule defect rather than an observed incident

incidents.title: A test's teardown emptied a shared server database, and a gate that never completed hid the red
incidents.rule: A test that mutates shared state must restore the baseline its successors expect (reset then reseed, never reset only), and the harness should re-establish and check that baseline when each shared step starts; a slow gate with no recorded completion since two tests landed has not tested them together, so treat the main line as unproven until it runs
incidents.signature: A late end-to-end step could not log in because an earlier test's teardown had deleted the seeded accounts from the shared server database.
incidents.root_cause: a test mutated shared state and restored an empty state instead of the baseline its successors expect, and the slow gate that would have run the two tests together had not completed since they were added
incidents.what: a full acceptance run passed every step through the server integration step and then failed two end-to-end tests with a login refusal. An earlier integration test shared the same server database and its teardown reset the content, deleting every collection except the framework's own, including the staff accounts. The end-to-end step then found no seeded account. Both tests were already on the main line; the records show no completed full run since they landed (that is the recorded history checked, not every historical run), so the red was latent there and was not caused by the change under review

incidents.title: A landing loop written for one shell's arrays ran under another and committed one of two files
incidents.rule: Iterate arrays with an explicit form valid in the running shell (the quoted all-elements expansion), and derive a commit message from the committed diff summary after the commit, not from intent
incidents.signature: A commit message claimed two files but only the first of the two was committed.
incidents.root_cause: the loop syntax was valid in the shell it was written for and silently different in the shell that ran it, and the commit message was written from intent instead of from the committed diff
incidents.what: a landing loop was written for one shell's array iteration (looping over an unquoted array variable) but ran under a different shell, which expands the unquoted variable to its first element only. One of two files was copied and committed, and the commit message claimed both. The operator caught it when the cleanup step could not find the second file on the main line; the missing file was then re-landed in its own commit

incidents.title: A module-presence guard went through the test's own file-system mock, so a missing-API label was never proven
incidents.rule: Before counting a red as missing-API, prove the guard both ways (module present: silent; module absent: fires), and never route a presence check through a mock the same test installs
incidents.signature: Tests labelled as missing-API reds still failed at the same guard after the module existed.
incidents.root_cause: a presence check was routed through a mock installed by the same test, and the red classification was accepted without observing the guard in both states (module present, module absent)
incidents.what: six tests were labelled missing-API reds at the first red stage. At the first green run they still failed at the same guard although the module existed. The guard checked module presence with a file-existence call, and the same test file replaced the file-system module with a mock that answered true only for one configuration string and false for the module's location. The guard therefore fired whether or not the module existed, and the missing-API label was never evidence. The green run showed four real behavioural gaps and six guard failures, with no genuine missing-API failure

incidents.title: A hand-written landing chain swallowed a failed post-commit leak scan and three commits landed on top
incidents.rule: Print the exit status of every commit and check step explicitly (never only on success), run the range leak scan before landing anything on top of a new commit, and use the guarded landing helper, not an ad-hoc chain
incidents.signature: A landing step printed nothing and the chain moved on, although the script it ran had exited non-zero.
incidents.root_cause: a post-commit check whose failure was swallowed by an output-printing chain, and an ad-hoc landing used in place of the guarded helper
incidents.what: a reviewer's file was landed with a hand-written chain: capture the output of a commit-and-check script, then print it only if the script succeeded. The script commits first and then runs a range leak scan, exiting 3 if the new commit leaks. It exited 3 because of a banned internal word in prose, the chain skipped the print, and nothing was shown. Three more commits were landed on top before a later range check flagged the first one. Pushes were frozen, so nothing left the machine. The guarded landing helper, which prints every step's status and stops on any failed check, was not used

incidents.title: A delegated test run needed login and logout, which delegates may not do, so the lead ran the pinned script
incidents.rule: When a test needs an action above a delegate's permission ceiling, the delegate writes and statically validates the script and pins its hash and exact command; the lead runs it unchanged and returns the artifacts; never weaken the test to fit the ceiling, and never let the delegate claim a result it did not observe
incidents.signature: A delegate prepared a browser walk that logs in and out but the runtime refused it for delegated agents.
incidents.root_cause: the test needed an action above the delegate's permission ceiling, and the delegate had no sanctioned route to the result other than the lead
incidents.what: a delegated QA agent prepared a browser click-around script that logs in as a test account, walks pages and logs out. The runtime classifies login and logout as externally visible writes and refuses them for delegated agents, so the delegate could not run its own script. The lead ran the exact script, pinned by its hash, under lead authority and handed the artifacts back for the report

incidents.title: A walk checklist attached another request variant's clause to the keyless request, so a correct response read as a failure
incidents.rule: Derive each checklist expectation verbatim from the delivered spec row and cite the row; triage every failure against the spec, the code and the active tests before calling it a defect
incidents.signature: A walk reported one failure on a response that matched the delivered spec.
incidents.root_cause: a checklist expectation was written from memory of the spec instead of copied from the delivered spec row, and mixed two request variants
incidents.what: the first milestone walk reported one failure. Triage against the delivered spec row showed the checklist had attached a clause meant for a different request variant (an empty-body not-found status for a wrong key) to the keyless request, which correctly returns the not-found view. The product was right and the checklist was a transcription error

incidents.title: A brief for a database-backed run omitted the test database endpoint, so the delegate rightly stopped
incidents.rule: A brief that asks for a runtime run must carry its runtime environment (the exact endpoint and environment variables, which slot is free, the load gate, and what must never be touched); a delegate that finds a required environment value missing stops and asks, never infers one
incidents.signature: A delegate stopped before a database-backed run and reported a missing environment variable.
incidents.root_cause: the brief named the runs but not the runtime environment they need, so the endpoint existed only in the lead's head
incidents.what: the lead asked a QA delegate to run database-backed full-tier test cases, but the brief did not give the dedicated test database endpoint. The delegate refused to guess one or to use a shared cluster, stopped, and reported the missing environment variable. The lead then supplied the endpoint and the run went ahead, costing one round trip

incidents.title: A new worktree symlinked its dependency trees to another worktree's, and the package manager relinked through them
incidents.rule: Never share a dependency tree between worktrees by symlink; give each worktree a private clone; never run the package manager unless the exact command is authorized; keep the verify-before-run settings off for every child; compare the full link inventory against a clean sibling after any suspected mutation
incidents.signature: A package manager command in one worktree changed the dependency links of another worktree.
incidents.root_cause: two worktrees shared one writable dependency tree by symlink, and the package manager's own freshness check treats the tree as its own to repair
incidents.what: a new worktree linked its three dependency roots (root, application, shared package) to another worktree's trees to avoid a copy. Its first package-manager command ran the tool's automatic freshness check, which relinked through those links: it retargeted the other worktree's workspace package link into the new worktree, re-hoisted two packages and rewrote shims and state files. The lead found it within minutes

incidents.title: A bare syntax check resolved to a different runtime that ignored the flag and executed the script
incidents.rule: Run syntax checks with the pinned binary by absolute path, and make every script that can act externally refuse at its first line without its required environment
incidents.signature: A syntax-check command executed the script it was meant only to parse.
incidents.root_cause: a bare command name was trusted to resolve to the pinned interpreter, and a flag was trusted to mean the same thing in whatever runtime answered
incidents.what: the lead syntax-checked a prepared browser walk script with a bare interpreter command and a check flag. In the tool shell the bare name resolved to a different runtime that ignores the flag and executes the file. The script's first statement refused because two required environment paths were unset, so nothing ran

incidents.title: A scrub command was refused as a broad home-directory scan by the operating system's privacy layer
incidents.rule: Scope searches to tracked files in your own tree; never scan the home directory
incidents.signature: A search step was refused by the operating system as a scan of the whole home directory.
incidents.root_cause: the search was scoped to a directory tree wider than the work, instead of to the tracked files of the teammate's own tree
incidents.what: a teammate's scrub command searched far beyond the teammate's own worktree and was refused by the operating system's privacy layer as a broad home-directory scan

incidents.title: A byte-count compare at the exact old length reported end of file on a prefix that matched
incidents.rule: Verify append-only files with an explicit byte-prefix compare, not a limited-length compare at the exact length
incidents.signature: A prefix check on an append-only file exited non-zero although the old bytes were unchanged.
incidents.root_cause: the check relied on a limited-length compare at the exact boundary, where the tool treats reaching the limit and end of file as a difference
incidents.what: a prefix check for an append-only file used the system compare tool limited to exactly the old file length. The BSD compare reported end of file and exited 1 even though the prefix matched, and an independent byte-prefix compare in a script showed the bytes identical

incidents.title: A test run's command-line exclusion flag did not take effect, so excluded cases ran and called the package manager
incidents.rule: List the collected files before a filtered run and stop if any excluded file is still collected
incidents.signature: Cases that were meant to be excluded from a run executed anyway.
incidents.root_cause: the exclusion was trusted from the flag instead of from the list of files actually collected before the run
incidents.what: a QA unit run used a command-line exclusion flag that did not take effect, so excluded resource-touching cases ran and their child processes called the package manager, against the rule that forbids it. The breach was disclosed in the review file

incidents.title: Two replies were stamped with times ahead of the clock
incidents.rule: Read the clock immediately before writing any timestamp, never estimate it
incidents.signature: Replies carried a time stamp later than the moment they were sent.
incidents.root_cause: the time stamps were estimated instead of read from the clock at the moment of writing
incidents.what: the lead stamped two replies with times ahead of the clock: both stamps were later than the real send time. The correction was recorded in the next ruling, and the content of the replies stood

incidents.title: A clause-survival script flagged 21 digest rules that a word diff showed were only wording compressions
incidents.rule: Run a word diff before treating a flagged rule as lost
incidents.signature: A clause-survival check flagged many rules as lost although their meaning was intact.
incidents.root_cause: the script compared surface words and treated any rewording as a missing clause
incidents.what: a clause-survival script flagged 21 digest rules as lost; a word diff showed each was only a wording compression, so no clause was missing

incidents.title: An engineer overwrote its own unit ledger with a later run
incidents.rule: Keep a ledger append-only with a dated section per run; never overwrite it with a later run
incidents.signature: A ledger file held only the latest run after an engineer wrote a new run over it.
incidents.root_cause: the ledger was written as a single current-state file instead of dated sections added at the end
incidents.what: an engineer overwrote its own unit ledger with the result of a later run, losing the earlier record

incidents.title: A signed design heading outranked a plan census parenthetical when two reviews disagreed on a file location
incidents.rule: When reviews disagree on a file location, read the signed design text first; it outranks a plan parenthetical
incidents.signature: Two reviews gave different locations for the same file.
incidents.root_cause: a secondary summary was weighed equally with the signed design text
incidents.what: two reviews disagreed on where a hook file lives: a signed low-level design heading (src/payload/hooks/) named one directory while a parenthetical in the plan census implied another; the lead ruled for the signed heading

incidents.title: A draft test root was revised in place after review, marker or activation
incidents.rule: Revise a draft test root in place only while it has no review, marker or activation; after that only a successor
incidents.signature: A root that others had reviewed or marked could be edited in place.
incidents.root_cause: the rule for when a draft stops being editable was not stated
incidents.what: a draft test root may be revised in place only while it has no review, marker or activation; once any of these exists a change must be a successor

incidents.title: A default that silently let a guard pass made a reviewer read a requirement as met
incidents.rule: A guard must fail closed with an explicit configuration error; never let a default make it pass
incidents.signature: A guard passed on an input it had never been told about.
incidents.root_cause: the default for an unknown slug was to allow, so a missing configuration looked like a pass
incidents.what: a default that silently lets a guard pass (a never-locked slug) led a reviewer to read a requirement as met, when nothing had been checked

incidents.title: Splitting a review's amendments kept the engineer busy while decisions were pending
incidents.rule: Split a review's amendments into apply-now and author-decides, and write no tests for undecided items early
incidents.signature: An engineer would have waited for all amendments of one review to be decided.
incidents.root_cause: amendments were treated as one batch rather than by who can decide them
incidents.what: a review's amendments were split between those the engineer applies now and those the spec author decides; the engineer stayed busy while decisions were pending, provided tests for undecided items were not written early

incidents.title: A landing helper's clean step deleted a pending root directory and left an unchanged tracked file deleted after the fast-forward
incidents.rule: A clean step must not leave a tracked unchanged file deleted; restore tracked files after a fast-forward and check tree status
incidents.signature: A tracked file that had not changed was gone after a landing.
incidents.root_cause: the clean step removed the whole directory, and the later fast-forward did not bring back files the revision left unchanged
incidents.what: a landing helper's clean step deleted the whole pending root directory in the author's worktree and then fast-forwarded, so an unchanged tracked file in an in-place revised root stayed deleted; the lead restored it

incidents.title: A whole-tree content digest detected a dependency change but could not say which file
incidents.rule: Record a marker-time file list as well as the whole-tree digest, so a change can be attributed to a file
incidents.signature: A digest differed from the marker value and gave no hint which file changed.
incidents.root_cause: only an aggregate digest was recorded at marker time, with no per-file before records
incidents.what: a whole-tree content digest detected a dependency-tree change but could not say which file changed, because per-file before records were not kept

incidents.title: A click-around walk that always exits 1 from a known gap cannot gate regressions
incidents.rule: Compare a walk with a known gap against a named baseline result; an exit code that is always failing cannot gate
incidents.signature: A walk reported failure on every run, so a new failure was indistinguishable.
incidents.root_cause: the gate used the exit code alone while a known gap kept it permanently failing
incidents.what: a click-around walk whose exit code is always 1 because of a declared, known gap could not gate regressions, since a new failure looked the same as the known one

incidents.title: A ruling was stamped four minutes ahead of the clock because the time was written before the clock was read
incidents.rule: Read the clock first, then write the time, in that order within the step
incidents.signature: A ruling carried a time stamp later than the moment it was written.
incidents.root_cause: the time was composed before the clock was read, even within one step
incidents.what: a ruling was stamped four minutes ahead of the clock because, in the same step, the time was written before the clock was read

incidents.title: The lead stamped a brief four minutes ahead of the clock again, one round after the same correction
incidents.rule: A failure that repeats after a written rule needs a mechanism: generate the time from the clock, never type it
incidents.signature: A brief carried a time stamp later than the moment it was written, after a rule against it was already recorded.
incidents.root_cause: the rule relied on the author remembering to read the clock; nothing enforced it
incidents.what: the lead stamped a brief four minutes ahead of the clock again, one round after the same failure was recorded; a repeated failure needs a mechanism, so the brief generator now writes the time from the clock

incidents.title: Two engineers answered the same STOP diagnosis independently, and agreeing answers let the lead route at once
incidents.rule: When a STOP cause is unknown, ask for two independent static answers before routing the fix
incidents.signature: A STOP had an unknown cause and a single diagnosis would have been unchecked.
incidents.root_cause: one answer to an unknown cause cannot be told apart from a plausible guess
incidents.what: two engineers answered the same STOP diagnosis independently and in parallel; their agreeing answers let the lead route the fix at once

incidents.title: A path-identity guard compared strings while a temp directory has two spellings on the host
incidents.rule: A path-identity guard compares real paths, never strings
incidents.signature: Two spellings of one directory compared unequal.
incidents.root_cause: the guard compared path strings and did not resolve symbolic prefixes
incidents.what: on this host a temp directory has two spellings, a symlinked prefix and its real path, so a path-identity guard that compared strings treated one directory as two

incidents.title: One review asked to delete an error-text assertion while another asked to pin the text
incidents.rule: Pin an error name, never message text, as the oracle
incidents.signature: Two reviews gave opposite instructions about the same assertion.
incidents.root_cause: message text was used as the oracle, so it was both brittle and the thing one review wanted pinned
incidents.what: one review asked to delete an error-text assertion while a second review asked to pin the text; the lead resolved both by pinning an error name and banning message-text oracles

incidents.title: A baseline comparison graded only rows present in the baseline, so a new failing row passed
incidents.rule: A baseline comparison must grade a row new in the run on its own outcome
incidents.signature: A run with a new failing row compared equal to its baseline.
incidents.root_cause: the comparison iterated over the baseline rows only, so rows absent from it were never graded
incidents.what: a baseline comparison graded only the rows present in the baseline, so a row new in the run that failed was not graded and the run passed

incidents.title: Two plan checks ran at a wrong script path and the last line of their output looked like a result
incidents.rule: Match the explicit pass line of a check, never its last line
incidents.signature: A crashed check ended with a line that resembled a result.
incidents.root_cause: only the last line was read, and a crash stack can end in a harmless looking line
incidents.what: the lead ran two plan checks at a wrong script path and read them through the last output line only; after a crash stack, the last line was just the runtime version line, which looked like output

incidents.title: A dispatch packet written for a future branch went stale when a later ruling started the work elsewhere
incidents.rule: Reconcile a dispatch packet with the newest ruling when it lands
incidents.signature: A packet named a branch and checkout that a later ruling had superseded.
incidents.root_cause: the packet was written ahead of time and not compared with the rulings made since
incidents.what: a dispatch packet written for a future branch went stale when a later ruling had already started the work on another checkout

incidents.title: An implementer's evidence admitted one case that contradicted its own every-undeclared-case-throws rule
incidents.rule: When evidence contradicts a stated rule, the rule wins: change the code, not the wording
incidents.signature: The evidence listed a case the stated rule said could not exist.
incidents.root_cause: the rule was weakened to match what the code did, instead of the code being fixed
incidents.what: an implementer's evidence admitted one case that contradicted its own rule that every undeclared case throws; the lead ruled that the rule wins and the code changes, not the wording

incidents.title: A declaration request that split sourced values from decisions let the lead rule eleven items in one pass
incidents.rule: Request declarations as sourced values and decisions, each with its gap
incidents.signature: A request mixed facts and open choices, which would have needed several rounds.
incidents.root_cause: facts and decisions were not separated, so each item needed triage before a ruling
incidents.what: a declaration request split sourced values from decisions, each with its gap, and the lead ruled eleven items in one pass

incidents.title: A load reading taken minutes before a launch was stale, and the launch read much higher
incidents.rule: Gate on load where you launch, immediately before; an earlier or second-hand reading is stale
incidents.signature: A load gate passed from a reading that no longer described the host.
incidents.root_cause: the reading was taken minutes earlier and by someone else, and load changes within minutes
incidents.what: a load reading taken minutes before a launch is stale: the lead's gate read low, the launch read far higher shortly after, and the engineer correctly refused the lead's reading as a substitute

incidents.title: A security predicate checked for truthiness failed open on an undefined or null value
incidents.rule: A security predicate allows only on the exact expected value, never on truthiness
incidents.signature: A guard allowed access when its input was missing.
incidents.root_cause: the predicate tested whether the value was truthy instead of whether it was the expected one
incidents.what: a security predicate checked for truthiness, so an undefined or null value failed open; fail closed means allowing only on the exact expected value

incidents.title: Handing a counting stream to a framework that catches stream failures lost the custom refusal contract
incidents.rule: Own the refusal contract before handing a stream to a framework that catches stream failures
incidents.signature: A custom refusal never reached the caller once the framework wrapped the stream.
incidents.root_cause: the refusal was raised inside the stream, where the framework catches failures
incidents.what: handing a counting stream to a framework that catches stream failures lost the custom refusal contract, because the framework turned the refusal into its own error

incidents.title: A multi-step command reported success for its later steps while its middle step had not happened
incidents.rule: Verify each landing by the commit log, never by the last line of the command
incidents.signature: A command's final output said done while one step had never run.
incidents.root_cause: success was read from the end of the command, and the middle step had failed silently
incidents.what: a multi-step command reported success for its later steps while its middle step, the plan commit, had not happened; this was found only by checking tree status after a context reset

incidents.title: A pending root whose supersession line said review pending failed the identity checker at landing
incidents.rule: Land a pending successor without its marker; write the marker only after the review
incidents.signature: The identity checker rejected a landing whose marker line said approval was pending.
incidents.root_cause: the marker was written before the review, so it asserted a state that did not exist
incidents.what: a pending root whose supersession approval line said review pending failed the identity checker at landing; the pending successor was landed without its marker, and the marker is to be written only after the review

incidents.title: A content inventory that hashed every file under the dependency tree stopped a clean run because the test runner rewrote its result cache there
incidents.rule: Exempt exactly one named path from a content inventory, with its digests recorded; never a directory or pattern
incidents.signature: An inventory guard failed a clean run because one cache file changed.
incidents.root_cause: the inventory covered every file in the tree, including one the runner is expected to rewrite
incidents.what: a content inventory that hashes every file under the dependency tree stopped a clean run, because the test runner rewrites its own result cache inside that tree; the fix exempts exactly one named path with its digests recorded, never a directory or pattern

incidents.title: A final review was reassigned from a busy reviewer to an idle one of a different model instead of queueing
incidents.rule: Reassign a review to an idle qualified reviewer of a different model rather than queueing it, keeping the non-author rule
incidents.signature: A review waiting for a busy reviewer would have stalled the acceptance step.
incidents.root_cause: the review was assigned to a named reviewer who was occupied
incidents.what: a final review was reassigned from a busy reviewer to an idle reviewer of a different model rather than queued behind the busy one; the author-independence rule still held

incidents.title: An activation instruction to delete superseded pending copies had nothing to delete because an earlier pure rename had already moved them
incidents.rule: Before a delete step in an activation, check the file exists; a prior pure rename leaves nothing to delete, so record that
incidents.signature: An instruction assumed pending copies still existed after they had been renamed away.
incidents.root_cause: the instruction was written from the expected state, not from the current tree
incidents.what: an activation instruction told the engineer to delete the superseded pending copies, but an earlier pure rename had already moved those files, so no deletion was needed

incidents.title: A dispatch packet called a root absent an hour after it had landed
incidents.rule: A conditional packet must re-read the newest main for every root it names before review
incidents.signature: A packet stated a root was absent when it was already present on main.
incidents.root_cause: the packet carried the state from when it was written and was not re-read against main
incidents.what: a dispatch packet called the r3 root absent an hour after it had landed on main

incidents.title: An author who received a ruling mid-run superseded its own earlier status with a dated addendum without rewriting the historical bytes
incidents.rule: When a ruling changes a status, append a dated addendum that supersedes it; never rewrite the historical bytes
incidents.signature: A status written before a ruling needed to change after it.
incidents.root_cause: the old status could only be changed by rewriting it, which would erase what was known at the time
incidents.what: an author who received a ruling mid-run appended a dated addendum that supersedes its own earlier status, and left the historical bytes unchanged

incidents.title: The identity checker allowed a successor root's new path with no predecessor line, and a marker maps only replaced paths
incidents.rule: A marker maps only replaced paths; a successor's new path needs no predecessor line
incidents.signature: A successor root added a path that had no earlier copy, and it was unclear whether a marker line was owed.
incidents.root_cause: the rule for new paths in a successor was not written down
incidents.what: the identity checker allows a successor root's new path with no predecessor line, because a marker maps only the paths it replaces

incidents.title: A safe default could silently drop data when an uncertain state was read as gone
incidents.rule: When a state is uncertain, treat the item as surviving; fail closed, never read a refusal as gone
incidents.signature: A safe default treated a refused read as an absent item.
incidents.root_cause: the decision on what an unreadable state means was not written down, so the default chose the destructive reading
incidents.what: a reviewer named a lead decision, that a permission error reads as the item being gone, on which a safe default could silently drop data; the lead ruled fail closed, so uncertain equals survivor

incidents.title: The demo server served a build made before the merge, so a walk after a source merge would have observed nothing new
incidents.rule: A milestone walk needs a fresh build of the merged SHA on its own port, never the running demo server
incidents.signature: A walk after a merge would have run against a server built before it.
incidents.root_cause: the running server reflects its build time, not the merged source
incidents.what: the demo server serves a build made before the merge and must not be touched, so a click-walk after a source merge would have observed nothing new

incidents.title: Two load readings around a sub-second run were equal because the host load average updates on a fixed interval
incidents.rule: Equal load readings around a sub-second run are expected from the fixed update interval; record each as read, never copy
incidents.signature: Two readings of host load were identical around a very short run.
incidents.root_cause: the load average updates on a fixed interval, longer than the run
incidents.what: two load readings taken around a sub-second run were equal because the host load average updates on a fixed interval; the lead's re-run showed the same, so equal readings are expected and were not copied

incidents.title: A lead signature line containing the assistant's product name failed the scrub
incidents.rule: Sign with a role name; a product name in a signature line fails the scrub
incidents.signature: A signature line failed the scrub.
incidents.root_cause: the signature used the product name instead of the role name
incidents.what: a lead signature line containing the assistant's product name failed the leak scrub

incidents.title: An evidence gap, a temporary config not retained, was closed by a lead re-run that kept it, not by asking the author to reconstruct it
incidents.rule: Close an evidence gap by a re-run that keeps and records the artifact, not by a reconstruction
incidents.signature: A run's evidence omitted a temporary config that had been deleted.
incidents.root_cause: the temporary file was removed after the run and not recorded
incidents.what: an evidence gap, that a temporary config was not retained, was closed by a lead re-run with the config kept and its content recorded, not by asking the author to reconstruct it

incidents.title: A landing helper's clean step fast-forwarded a merged feature branch's ref, which would have moved a live branch
incidents.rule: A clean step must never move a branch ref that is still under work
incidents.signature: A clean step changed the ref of a branch that had already been merged, and it could have been one still in use.
incidents.root_cause: the clean step moved every listed branch to main without checking whether any was still under work
incidents.what: the landing helper's clean step fast-forwarded a merged feature branch's ref to main; harmless after the merge, but it would have moved a branch still under work

incidents.title: The lead re-merged the full candidate itself rather than queue behind the busy owner, and proved the delta path by path
incidents.rule: When the owner is busy, redo a mechanical merge directly and prove the new delta equals the old path by path
incidents.signature: A mechanical merge was waiting for a busy owner.
incidents.root_cause: the work was assigned to its original owner by default
incidents.what: the lead re-merged the full candidate itself rather than queue behind the busy owner, and proved that the new candidate's delta equals the old one path by path

incidents.title: A red phase may start while a spec recheck runs because the reviewed bytes fix the behavior
incidents.rule: Start the red phase while a spec recheck runs; only the production commit waits
incidents.signature: Work waited for a recheck that could not change the reviewed behavior.
incidents.root_cause: the dependency was treated as all or nothing instead of by what the recheck could change
incidents.what: a red phase of activation, an inert stub and engineer tests may start while a spec recheck runs, because the reviewed test bytes fix the behavior; only the production commit waits

incidents.title: A whole-unit re-run showed five failures in unrelated files because a required environment variable was unset in the shell
incidents.rule: Record failures caused by an unset environment variable as an environment gap, never a pass and never a regression
incidents.signature: A whole-unit run failed in files unrelated to the change under acceptance.
incidents.root_cause: the shell lacked a required variable, and the guards failed closed as designed
incidents.what: the lead's whole-unit re-run for an acceptance showed 5 failures in files that import none of the code under acceptance, all failing closed because the test database admin URL was unset in that shell; the acceptance document recorded them as an environment gap, never as a pass and never as a regression

incidents.title: An acceptance document cited a ruling that did not yet exist when it was signed
incidents.rule: A signed record cites only rulings that exist, or says the item is to be ruled
incidents.signature: A signed record referred to a ruling that was not yet written.
incidents.root_cause: the ruling was expected and cited as if it had been made
incidents.what: an acceptance document cited a ruling that did not yet exist when it was signed

incidents.title: A static package-constant check before dispatch found a design constant absent on main
incidents.rule: Before dispatch, check statically that every constant and export the design names exists on main
incidents.signature: A design named a constant that the code on main did not export.
incidents.root_cause: the design was written ahead of the code that would export the constant
incidents.what: a static package-constant check before dispatch found that the design's upload constant was absent on main, which turned a predictable runtime import failure into a planning fact

incidents.title: A ruling timestamp was written from an estimate and corrected minutes later, twice in one round
incidents.rule: Read the clock immediately before writing each timestamp; never write one from an estimate
incidents.signature: A ruling carried a time that did not match the clock.
incidents.root_cause: the time was written from an estimate instead of from a fresh clock read
incidents.what: the lead wrote two ruling timestamps from an estimate rather than the clock and corrected them minutes later

incidents.title: Ten teammate threads showed state paused with complete outputs on disk and no reply message
incidents.rule: Grade a teammate output from the file on disk; a missing reply or a paused state is not a verdict
incidents.signature: A thread showed paused and sent no reply while its output file was complete.
incidents.root_cause: the thread state and the reply channel do not reliably report that the work is finished
incidents.what: ten teammate threads showed state paused with complete outputs on disk and no reply message; the lead graded each output from the file, never from a missing reply

incidents.title: A load gate read and a launch chained in one command let a unit probe start at a load above the gate
incidents.rule: Run the load read and the launch as two separate commands; a reading at or above the gate stops the launch
incidents.signature: A probe started on a host whose load was far above the gate.
incidents.root_cause: the gate read and the launch were chained, so the chained launch ran whatever the read showed
incidents.what: a load gate read and a launch chained in one command let a unit probe start at load1 42.87, above the unit gate of 24; the breach was recorded, not hidden, and the result stood only as a suite-level module error

incidents.title: The milestone runbook shell-sourced an environment file and failed before the build on a value with angle brackets
incidents.rule: Read an environment file line by line, never shell-source it; a value with angle brackets breaks sourcing
incidents.signature: The runbook failed at its first step on a value the shell parsed as syntax.
incidents.root_cause: the shell interpreted characters inside a value as syntax
incidents.what: the milestone runbook shell-sourced an environment file and failed before the build on a value with angle brackets; reading the file line by line fixed it

incidents.title: A registry edit failed its own sorted-order assertion, and the identity checker refuses a supersession whose old path the registry still names
incidents.rule: Change the registry line and the supersession record whose old path it names in one control commit, and assert the sorted order first
incidents.signature: A registry edit and a supersession record conflicted when landed separately.
incidents.root_cause: the registry and the supersession record each constrain the other, so neither can land first
incidents.what: the lead's registry edit first failed its own sorted-order assertion, and the identity checker refuses a SUPERSEDES whose old path is still named by the registry; both files change in one control commit

incidents.title: A reviewer finding moved a hook registration owner twice in one hour
incidents.rule: Assign a hook registration owner only after reading which row owns the hook's neighbours
incidents.signature: The owner of one registration changed twice in about an hour.
incidents.root_cause: the first owner was chosen before the neighbouring rows were read
incidents.what: a reviewer's finding moved a hook registration owner twice in one hour (T05a, then T05b, then L4-T03); the owner was fixed only after reading which row owns the hook's neighbours

incidents.title: A closure packet freeze test turned positive on a control-only landing and the lead admitted it narrowly
incidents.rule: Admit a freeze-test hit only narrowly: name the landing, why the run cannot read it, and the change that makes it a new STOP; never waive the identity step
incidents.signature: A freeze test reported a change that the guarded run could not read.
incidents.root_cause: the freeze test checks main, while the run reads its own detached copy of the registry and markers
incidents.what: the closure packet's freeze test turned positive on a control-only landing that changed checker metadata on main and nothing the run reads; the lead admitted it narrowly for the diagnostic-only run because the run executes in a detached clone with its own registry and markers, any further change to a registry or marker file before launch is a new STOP, and the identity step is not waived

incidents.title: A scoped compiler config flagged an import style that the canonical build never compiles
incidents.rule: Check a scoped compiler diagnostic against the canonical build before calling it a defect; fix a scoped-config artifact in the retained config, not the repository
incidents.signature: A scoped compile failed on a file the canonical build does not compile.
incidents.root_cause: the scoped config includes files the canonical build never reaches
incidents.what: a scoped compiler config reported an error on an import style that six helpers on main already use, because the canonical build compiles only its referenced projects and never reaches that file; the lead allowed the option in the external retained config only, with no repository config change and no test change

incidents.title: A review was reassigned off the critical path so the reviewer who owned the blocking recheck stayed on it
incidents.rule: Keep the reviewer on the critical path on that path and reassign off-path reviews to another non-author
incidents.signature: One reviewer held two reviews while a blocking recheck waited.
incidents.root_cause: the first assignment ignored which reviewer owned the blocking recheck
incidents.what: a production diff review was reassigned from the reviewer who held the blocking design recheck to a different reviewer, so the critical path stayed with its owner and the diff was still reviewed by a non-author

incidents.title: A captions upload relation in a spec would have added a media referrer to a collection defined as image-only
incidents.rule: Before adding a relation to a shared collection, check what the collection holds and which referrer lists it joins; defer and record a gap if it does not fit
incidents.signature: A relation targeted a collection that does not accept its content.
incidents.root_cause: the relation was specified from the field's purpose without checking the target collection's scope
incidents.what: a spec proposed a captions upload relation to the media collection, but media is image-only with fixed upload limits, so the relation would have added a media referrer to the lists of an earlier row; the lead deferred the file subfield to the later caption and video upload work and recorded the gap

incidents.title: A framework operation order showed that file data is generated before the field validators, so a security check moved to the operation hook
incidents.rule: Place a security check on original input in a hook that runs before the framework transforms the input, verified in the installed source, and record any move as a named deviation
incidents.signature: A content check ran after the framework had already rewritten the input it was meant to inspect.
incidents.root_cause: the design assumed a hook order that the installed framework does not have
incidents.what: the design placed the upload content sniff in the field-validation hook, but the installed framework source shows that file data generation can replace the file type and decode the upload before any field validator runs; the engineer's correction was verified at line level in the installed source and the sniff moved to the operation hook, ahead of generation, inspecting the original bytes, with the file-size guard first

incidents.title: A generated migration needed a lint-only edit, so the evidence carries the raw and delivered hashes and the one-line diff
incidents.rule: When a generated file needs a lint-only edit, change only the named defect and record the raw hash, the delivered hash and the diff
incidents.signature: A generated file failed lint while its content was correct.
incidents.root_cause: the generator emits names the lint rules reject
incidents.what: a generated migration failed lint on unused destructured names; the lead allowed removing only those names in the up and down functions, with the SQL, the snapshot and every other byte as generated, and required the evidence to record the raw and delivered hashes of the file and the one-line diff for each function

incidents.title: A host load spike came from operating system daemons, not the team, and the load wait held
incidents.rule: A load gate holds regardless of who causes the load; continue static work and do not touch system daemons
incidents.signature: Host load was far above the gate while no team run was active.
incidents.root_cause: operating system daemons raised the load without any team action
incidents.what: host load1 read 131.65, driven by operating system background daemons and not by any teammate run; the load wait applied to every run, static work continued, and the lead did not touch the system daemons

incidents.title: A supersession marker was deferred to each row's activation because writing it now would trip the freeze test
incidents.rule: Defer a marker or registry change that would trip an active freeze test to the activation step, and name the approval it will cite
incidents.signature: A control write was due while a freeze condition forbade control changes.
incidents.root_cause: the marker is needed later but an admission forbids any such change now
incidents.what: the supersession chains for the locator successors were not written now but at each row's activation map, because under the standing narrow admission any marker or registry change on main before the diagnostic launch is a new STOP; the reviewer's approval that the markers will cite is already on disk

incidents.title: A dependency question was answered by the backlog itself, a relation owned by a later row, so no wait was needed
incidents.rule: Before waiting on a dependency, read the backlog for the row that owns it; if a later row owns it, ship without it and add no stub
incidents.signature: A spec raised a wait on something a later row was already scheduled to add.
incidents.root_cause: the spec did not check which row owns the relation
incidents.what: a spec asked whether to wait for a relation to sponsorship data, and the lead answered from the backlog: a later row adds that relation, so this row ships without it and no stub collection is created; it is not a deviation from the cut

incidents.title: A route validator rejected a width that the generator was required to emit
incidents.rule: Check every producer output against every consumer validator before signing a design, with a control for the edge output and for each refused value
incidents.signature: A consumer refused a value that its own producer was required to emit.
incidents.root_cause: the validator and the generator were specified separately and never compared on the edge case
incidents.what: the spec's route validator accepted only the standard rendition widths, while the generator must emit a smaller fallback width when the crop is under the smallest standard width; the lead sanctioned a syntactic width rule (a standard width or a canonical integer in the fallback range), with served files still limited to those the generator stored, and required controls for the under-size fixture and for rejected widths

incidents.title: Interim content was signed as clearly marked placeholder copy instead of being invented as sourced
incidents.rule: Sign interim content as a visibly marked placeholder with its open question and owner; never present an invented value as sourced
incidents.signature: Seed content needed text that no source provided.
incidents.root_cause: the inventory had gaps that only the content owner can fill
incidents.what: for seed content with no sourced text, the lead signed deterministic interim copy that carries a visible placeholder suffix, and interim labels recorded as a content-owner question rather than a sourced fact; the open item stays open for real copy and no synthesized marketing text is written

incidents.title: Hand delivery under a hold, with one reconciliation after the load, replaced blocking on a state flip
incidents.rule: Under a held state flip, deliver by hand on the established precedent and reconcile once after the hold; keep every freeze rule
incidents.signature: Three rows waited on a backlog state flip that was held on purpose.
incidents.root_cause: the flip depends on an event that is not on the critical path
incidents.what: with the backlog state flip held until a later load, the design conditions for three rows were met, so the lead adopted hand delivery as the operating mode: implement on branches and merge by hand as for earlier rows, record the backlog state for every hand-merged row in one reconciliation after the load, regenerate the dependent patch on the real post-load base with a non-author re-review, and keep the freeze admission rules for any registry or marker change

incidents.title: A job text swapped two commit identities, and reading the log caught it
incidents.rule: Read the log for every commit a job text names before acting on it, and record the correction
incidents.signature: Two commits were named the wrong way round in an instruction.
incidents.root_cause: the identities were written from memory of the order instead of from the log
incidents.what: a job text swapped the identities of two commits (the two sub-items were named the wrong way round); the lead read the commit log, noted which commit is which sub-item in the ruling, and followed the log

incidents.title: A reviewer's framework claim was corrected from the installed source: a draft save writes only the versions table
incidents.rule: Verify a reviewer's framework claim in the installed source before adopting it, and cite the source
incidents.signature: A reviewer stated a framework behavior that the installed source does not show.
incidents.root_cause: the claim was made from memory of the framework, not from the installed version
incidents.what: a reviewer's claim about what a draft save writes was corrected from the installed framework source: a draft save writes only the versions table

incidents.title: A low-load window needed immediate dispatch of the gated runs
incidents.rule: When a low-load window opens, dispatch the gated runs at once, reading the load in its own command before each launch
incidents.signature: Gated runs waited while a short low-load window was open.
incidents.root_cause: the window is brief and unpredictable, and the gated runs are not started on their own
incidents.what: a low-load window opened for the runs held behind the load gate, and the lead dispatched them immediately because the window is short and the gate must be read immediately before each launch

incidents.title: A squash recipe equated the landing tree with a stale branch tree and would have dropped later main work
incidents.rule: A squash landing tree must equal the merge result of the pinned main and the branch head, never the branch tree; rebuild when main moves
incidents.signature: A landing recipe that would have silently removed work already on main.
incidents.root_cause: the recipe compared the landing with the branch alone, which ignores everything main gained after the branch point
incidents.what: a squash landing recipe required the landing commit's tree to equal the branch's final tree, but the branch predated later main landings, so that tree would have dropped main content; a reviewer caught the seam and the lead withdrew the clause: the squash tree must equal the conflict-free merge result, printed by the merge-tree command with both commit ids pinned in the message, and a stale tree is never reused after main moves

incidents.title: Evidence receipts leaked absolute paths into branch history, and the lead landed by squash instead of rewriting history
incidents.rule: Write evidence commands with placeholders for paths and tools; handle leaked history by a squash landing that keeps the original branch as the local audit trail
incidents.signature: The leak guard reported absolute paths and a tool name inside evidence files.
incidents.root_cause: receipts recorded the literal command lines of the run
incidents.what: thirteen leak-guard hits were absolute home paths and a tool name in the recorded commands of an evidence file; the lead had the engineer rewrite the file without them, noting that earlier receipts carry literal paths in branch history, and landed through a squash so the leaking history is not merged, keeping the original branch local as the audit trail, never pushed or deleted

incidents.title: A lint rule against a throw inside a finally block caught a real defect in production code
incidents.rule: Treat a lint error as a defect: restructure, pin each intended behavior with a unit case, and add no disable comment or rule change
incidents.signature: A final lint gate failed on code that looked finished.
incidents.root_cause: a release failure was handled by throwing inside a finally block, which can replace the original outcome
incidents.what: the final lint gate exited non-zero on two errors in a request-size helper, a dead assignment and a throw inside a finally block; the lead ruled both real production defects, fixed in one commit with the intended behaviors each pinned by a unit case and no disable comment or rule change

incidents.title: A generated down migration dropped a table with cascade and then dropped the removed constraint again
incidents.rule: Fix a generated down migration by a minimal named edit with raw and delivered hashes, and report it as static until a round trip proves it
incidents.signature: A down migration contained a statement that fails after an earlier statement had already removed its target.
incidents.root_cause: the generator emits a cascade drop and an explicit constraint drop for the same object
incidents.what: a generated down migration dropped the media table with cascade, which already removes the referencing foreign key, and then dropped that same constraint, so the down step would fail with constraint does not exist; the lead sanctioned a hand edit of that one statement to drop the constraint only if it exists, recorded the raw and delivered hashes, and treated the fix as static until a round trip crosses it

incidents.title: An image library throw on undecodable bytes surfaced as a server error instead of a refusal
incidents.rule: Catch a library throw on untrusted input and refuse with a client error status and a stable reason code; pin it with a valid-signature, bad-body case
incidents.signature: Malformed upload bytes produced a server error.
incidents.root_cause: the signature check passed, so the decoder was assumed to succeed
incidents.what: the image metadata call could throw on bytes that pass the signature check but do not decode, which would surface as a server error; the lead ruled to catch the throw and refuse with a client error status and a fixed reason code, never to swallow it, with a unit case of a valid signature followed by garbage

incidents.title: A geometry spec's rounded intermediate broke a test tolerance, caught by independent arithmetic
incidents.rule: Recompute spec geometry independently against the oracle tolerance, round at the last step, and never loosen the oracle
incidents.signature: A spec's numbers did not meet the test tolerance they were written for.
incidents.root_cause: a rounded intermediate value was reused downstream and the error added up
incidents.what: a reviewer recomputed the rendition geometry independently and found that a rounded intermediate would have produced an output height off by more than the oracle's tolerance of one pixel; the lead kept the rounded extract rectangle, set the output height by rounding width over the ratio, made the resize exact, accepted a sub-pixel stretch of at most one pixel, and recomputed every row without loosening the tolerance

incidents.title: The lead wrote a ruling timestamp before reading the clock
incidents.rule: Read the clock immediately before writing each timestamp; write the time after the read, not before
incidents.signature: A ruling carried a time written before the clock was read.
incidents.root_cause: the time was written before the clock read, the same cause as earlier cases
incidents.what: the lead wrote a ruling timestamp before reading the clock

incidents.title: A self-imposed freeze outlived its reason and was blocking three rows' activations
incidents.rule: Re-derive a freeze's mechanism before honoring it; withdraw it when the guarded run cannot read what it protects
incidents.signature: A STOP kept blocking work after the run it protected could no longer be affected.
incidents.root_cause: the freeze was honored as a rule after the reason for it had changed
incidents.what: a self-imposed freeze (a main-side STOP on registry and marker changes) was kept after its reason was gone: the guarded run read only its own detached clone with its own registry and markers, so a change on main could not affect it, yet the freeze was blocking the activations of three rows; the lead re-derived the mechanism, withdrew the STOP and lifted the marker deferral

incidents.title: A static closure packet that did not converge in three rounds was replaced by running the thing and diagnosing the receipts
incidents.rule: When a static closure packet does not converge in three rounds, replace it by running the thing on current code and diagnosing the receipts
incidents.signature: Static review rounds kept finding the same open items.
incidents.root_cause: a census by reading cannot settle what only a run shows
incidents.what: a static closure packet for a heavy run did not converge in three review rounds, with the same closure items still partly open, and the target had also gone stale against newer main; the lead retired it and ruled to run the regression tier on current main, keeping the reusable parts and diagnosing any unexpected failure from the run's own receipts instead of a deep static census

incidents.title: A migration lock covered the whole branch when it needed to cover only the generators and schema paths
incidents.rule: Scope a lock to the shared paths and commands it protects, not the whole branch, and state how a second branch rejoins after the holder merges
incidents.signature: A second branch idled although most of its work did not touch the locked resource.
incidents.root_cause: the lock was defined by the branch instead of by the resource
incidents.what: the migration lock was read as covering a whole branch, so a second branch could not proceed at all; the lead narrowed it to the generators, the migration and generated-types paths and any run that needs the new schema, so a second branch may author code and tests, activate files and run its red phase in parallel, then merges main, generates on that base and sorts after the holder, with a snapshot whose parent is not the latest migration on main a STOP

incidents.title: A fresh worktree can be provisioned by a copy-on-write clone of the dependency tree instead of an install that may hit dead store links
incidents.rule: Provision a fresh worktree by a copy-on-write clone of the dependency tree, never by linking, when an install may hit dead store links
incidents.signature: An offline install failed on dead links in the package store.
incidents.root_cause: the store links an install depends on can be dead, while a copied tree carries relative links
incidents.what: a fresh worktree can be provisioned with a copy-on-write clone copy of the dependency tree, because the package manager's links are relative, instead of an install that may hit dead store links

incidents.title: Tests authored but never executed passed acceptance, and the first run of the heavy tier found a failing case
incidents.rule: Accept a production merge only after the heavy test tier passes on the merged tree; authored but unexecuted cases are missing evidence, not a pass
incidents.signature: A row was signed off with part of its tests never run.
incidents.root_cause: the acceptance gates did not include the tier that held the row's heaviest cases
incidents.what: a row was accepted on unit, type and lint checks while its ten heavy-tier cases were recorded as authored, not executed; the first run of the heavy tier on the merged tree found one failing case (G08), a test defect: the framework's bulk update computes one generated file once and reuses it for every target, so a two-target bulk replacement gave both documents the same filename; the lead fixed the test on a branch and ruled that from the next row on a production merge is accepted only after the heavy tier passes on the merged tree, added to the other gates and not substituted for them

incidents.title: Two fields mapping to one database enum made the generated migration narrow a five-state status to two states
incidents.rule: Give each field that persists a state set its own enum name per table, and check the generated SQL for every state before generating types
incidents.signature: A generated migration silently narrowed a status to fewer states than the field allows.
incidents.root_cause: two fields mapped to the same default enum name, so the first definition won
incidents.what: the framework's own draft status field and the persistent five-state status field collided on one generated enum name, so the generated migration gave both the two draft states and would have rejected the other three; the engineer caught it by reading the generated SQL before type generation and stopped; the lead sourced a per-field enum-name option in the installed packages and ruled a distinct enum name per table for the persistent field, with the generated files removed by exact name and regenerated, and a check before type generation that all five states are present on both persistent enums

incidents.title: The lead missed six teammate replies across a context compaction and left the critical-path engineer idle for 35 minutes
incidents.rule: Check thread activity right after every context compaction, before any other step
incidents.signature: Replies sat unread after a compaction.
incidents.root_cause: the compaction dropped the lead's awareness of pending replies and nothing prompted a re-check
incidents.what: after a context compaction the lead missed replies from six teammates, which finished between 04:29 and 04:45 and were seen at 05:05 through the activity listing; the critical-path engineer had a stop waiting and sat idle for 35 minutes

incidents.title: A load gate stop was the right call and cost nothing because the runner created nothing before the check
incidents.rule: Put the load check before anything is created, so a gate stop costs nothing and leaves nothing to tear down
incidents.signature: A run stopped at the gate while the host was overloaded.
incidents.root_cause: host load rose from processes outside the team
incidents.what: the runner of a milestone walk stopped at its first step because host load read 48.87 and then 38.48, above the gate, with nothing created and nothing to tear down; the load came from processes outside the team, which nobody touches; the lead called the stop correct and re-dispatches the walk when the gate reads low

incidents.title: The lead missed eight teammate replies with no compaction and saw them only through thread activity
incidents.rule: Check thread states after every landing batch, not only after a context compaction
incidents.signature: Replies were missing from the lead view while the work sat finished.
incidents.root_cause: the lead checked for lost replies only after compactions
incidents.what: eight teammates finished between 05:11 and 05:21 and the lead saw the replies only through the thread activity listing, although no context compaction had happened

incidents.title: A ruling cannot override a teammate tool rules, so the lead sleep loop load waiter was refused and withdrawn
incidents.rule: Wait for load with an event driven observer owned by the lead, never a sleep loop in a teammate; a ruling does not override a teammate tool rules
incidents.signature: A ruled helper was refused by the teammate it was meant for.
incidents.root_cause: the ruled helper needed an action the teammate tool rules forbid
