incidents.what: the lead ruled a load wait helper built as a sleep loop, and the runner was right to refuse it because teammate tool rules forbid sleep loops and a ruling does not override those rules; the helper was withdrawn

incidents.title: Teammates cannot remove or drop, so teardown belongs to the lead and runs from the runner names file
incidents.rule: Plan teardown as a lead owned step driven from the runner names file, and keep walk pass and cleanup pass separate
incidents.signature: Cleanup could not be run by the teammate that created the things.
incidents.root_cause: teammate permissions exclude removal and drop operations
incidents.what: teammates cannot run removals or database drops because of their permission ceiling; for a walk the runner stops after copying its evidence and writes a names file, and the lead runs teardown from that file: stop the server by its recorded process id, drop the database under an exact name guard, dump it, and remove the root and worktree; the lead appends a clocked receipt to the runner report and walk pass and cleanup pass stay separate

incidents.title: A file creation mask from an earlier tool call did not carry over, and the database dump came out world readable
incidents.rule: Set the mask, run, and assert the result in one command, because shell state does not carry across tool calls
incidents.signature: A dump file was readable by others for a short time.
incidents.root_cause: shell state from an earlier call was assumed to persist
incidents.what: a file creation mask set in an earlier tool call did not carry into a fresh shell, so the database dump tool wrote the custom format dump with mode 644 inside a 700 root; the runner mode assertion at its fourth step caught it, stopped correctly, created no database, and tightened the mode to 600 at once

incidents.title: A provenance check that the generator can never satisfy: the zero parent id on every snapshot
incidents.rule: Prove a diff base from what the generated SQL does and does not emit, and never demand a check the generator can not satisfy
incidents.signature: A required check was impossible to pass whatever the code did.
incidents.root_cause: the check was written from an assumption about the generator output
incidents.what: a parent id equality check for a snapshot could never pass, because the installed generator gives every snapshot the zero parent id, including the default one, the adapter default snapshot and the accepted prior migration; the check was withdrawn

incidents.title: The lead wrote ruling timestamps from memory three times and had to correct them
incidents.rule: Compute a timestamp from the clock in the same command that writes it, never from memory
incidents.signature: Timestamps in rulings were wrong until corrected.
incidents.root_cause: times were typed from estimates
incidents.what: the lead wrote ruling timestamps from memory three times and corrected each one afterwards

incidents.title: A ruling wrote a media directory binding from memory that contradicted the pinned scripts, and the runner stopped instead of substituting
incidents.rule: Check a binding against the pinned scripts before writing it, and stop on a contradiction rather than substitute
incidents.signature: A written binding contradicted the scripts it was meant to drive.
incidents.root_cause: the binding was written from memory
incidents.what: a ruling wrote the media directory binding from memory and it contradicted the pinned helper and walker scripts and the earlier ruling for that step; the runner stopped rather than substitute, and the next ruling corrected the binding to the media folder under the walk root exactly, with no symlink, while the other overrides stood; the lead said the runner was right to stop

incidents.title: A generated down migration defect fixed once came back in the next row because the fix was never turned into a check
incidents.rule: Turn a fixed generator defect into a check on the list that every later generated migration runs
incidents.signature: A defect already fixed once appeared again with no check to catch it.
incidents.root_cause: a one time fix was recorded as a ruling but not added to a list of checks
incidents.what: the generated down migration dropped a table with cascade and then dropped the removed constraint without if exists, which fails; it was found and fixed by a sanctioned edit in one row, and the same defect appeared again in the next row and was found only by a static review, because the fix had not been turned into a check that every generated migration runs

incidents.title: A new required argument broke an older direct caller that the change did not list
incidents.rule: When an argument becomes required, list every direct caller, tests included, and keep the old call path or update every caller in the same change
incidents.signature: A whole unit run showed one more failure after a signature change.
incidents.root_cause: the new argument was checked against new callers only
incidents.what: a change made a finite clock argument required; a seed test that called the function directly the older way failed as a sixth whole unit failure, because the change had been checked against the new callers only; the repair kept the legacy call path working

incidents.title: An order sensitive comparison of two tool listings failed only when new files were added, though the contract was set membership
incidents.rule: Compare sorted copies when the contract is set membership, and keep order sensitive equality for contracts that define order
incidents.signature: A test failed after unrelated files were added.
incidents.root_cause: the assertion was stricter than the contract it was named for
incidents.what: a test compared two listings from a test tool with an order sensitive equality, while its name and contract said every ordinary file is kept, which is set membership; it passed until new model files changed the listing order and then failed with no product change

incidents.title: A hook ran a query on create with an undefined id once a registry became non empty: a latent defect exposed by data, not code
incidents.rule: Guard a hook query on the operation and a valid id; a check over an empty population proves nothing about the non empty case
incidents.signature: A seed failed with a database type error after a data change.
incidents.root_cause: the query path was never exercised while the registry was empty
incidents.what: a before change hook ran a referrer count with an undefined document id on a create; the count became NaN and the database refused it with an invalid text representation error as soon as a registry that had been empty gained entries; the defect was latent from the earlier row and was exposed by the later row, not by any code change

incidents.title: An identity guard compared to a plain address while the database cast rendered the address with a mask, so it could never pass, and a silent catch hid which check failed
incidents.rule: Probe a guard against the real value it will see; a guard that can never pass is a defect, and a catch must print which step failed without secrets
incidents.signature: A walk stopped at its helper with one generic error.
incidents.root_cause: the guard was written against an assumed rendering of the value
incidents.what: a helper and a walker bound the database identity by comparing the text cast of the server address, which renders with a /32 suffix, to the plain address, so the guard could never pass; a catch in the helper reported one generic error and hid which step failed; it stopped a run before any change and was found by a read only query

incidents.title: A subprocess call failed with not found when the pinned runtime directory was missing from the search path, and the first run showed five extra failures
incidents.rule: Put the pinned runtime directory on the search path in the same command that runs the tests; a not found error from a spawned tool is an environment fault, not a product failure
incidents.signature: Extra failures appeared in the first run.
incidents.root_cause: the test shell did not carry the runtime search path
incidents.what: a test spawned the package manager and failed with a not found error because the directory of the pinned runtime was not on the search path; the first run showed five extra failures that were not product defects

incidents.title: Color escape codes in a report broke an extraction assertion, and only the zero match assertion caught it
incidents.rule: Strip terminal escape codes before parsing a report, and keep a zero match assertion so a failed extraction writes nothing
incidents.signature: An extraction found no matches in a report that held the text.
incidents.root_cause: escape codes sat inside the text being matched
incidents.what: a script that extracted counts from a report failed because the report carried terminal color escape codes; no bytes were written, because the zero match assertion stopped it before the write

incidents.title: An admission sent at a low load reading reached the runner after the load rose again, and the runner fresh reading then refused it
incidents.rule: An admission admits the step: a reading within 60 seconds of the admission is a record, and a reading after that is a fresh gate
incidents.signature: A runner refused a step that had just been admitted.
incidents.root_cause: the admission and the runner reading were two gates a minute apart on a host whose load swings fast
incidents.what: an admission was sent at a low load reading, but it reached the runner after the window closed and the load had risen by about ten within a minute; the runner read load fresh at its first step, saw a value above the gate and refused; the refusal was correct under the rule as written, and the cause was the gap between the admission and the reading

incidents.title: A script carried internal load vetoes that contradicted a later decision, and the script bytes were immutable
incidents.rule: When a ruling changes a gate, list every script that encodes the old gate before the ruling is relied on
incidents.signature: A script stopped a run on a gate that a ruling had removed.
incidents.root_cause: the ruling changed the gate in text, and the gate also lived in script bytes
incidents.what: a walker script held two internal load vetoes, a start gate and a browser start gate, that contradicted a later ruling to record load and not stop; they would have blocked the walker right after a build; the runner refused to edit bytes that were pinned as immutable, and the lead issued a successor script that prints a recorded only marker at both places and changes nothing else

incidents.title: A run plan barred the test author from running the script, and a later message assigned that author anyway
incidents.rule: Check an assignment against the independence rules of the plan before sending it
incidents.signature: A message contradicted the plan it was meant to follow.
incidents.root_cause: the assignment was written without reading the independence rule in the plan
incidents.what: a run plan barred the author of the tests from running the walk, and a later lead message assigned that author to run it anyway; the author of the walker script caught the conflict before the run; the independence rule stood, and a runner who authored neither code nor tests was named

incidents.title: A helper finished its work but hung in the framework shutdown call, and its pass line came after the shutdown, so no evidence printed
incidents.rule: Write the evidence line before any shutdown call, bound the shutdown with a timeout, and exit explicitly
incidents.signature: A step did its work and then sat idle with no output.
incidents.root_cause: the pass line was written after a shutdown call that can wait forever
incidents.what: a helper set a password and wrote its credentials file, then hung for about ten minutes in the framework shutdown call, whose pool waited on a connection that was never released; its pass line was written after the shutdown, so no evidence printed; the lead diagnosed it read only from the file modification time, the row update time and an idle database session, and then stopped the exact recorded process id

incidents.title: A long acceptance run launched with a detached command inside a subshell from a tool shell never started, and no output file existed minutes later
incidents.rule: Launch a long run as a tracked background task, and check that its first output file exists right after the launch
incidents.signature: A launched run left no output and no process.
incidents.root_cause: the launch form was not one the tool shell supports, and no check followed it
incidents.what: the lead launched an acceptance run with a detached command inside a subshell from a tool shell; the run never started and no output file existed minutes later, because nothing checked that the launch had produced a first output file

incidents.title: A count change in an acceptance document was attributed to specific items without a per file check
incidents.rule: State a count delta with its base commit, and attribute it to a row only after a per file check
incidents.signature: A count change was credited to rows with no per file evidence.
incidents.root_cause: the attribution was inferred from the total, not from the files
incidents.what: an acceptance document first attributed a change in test counts to specific rows without checking per file; the lead amended it before anyone used it

incidents.title: Drafts proposed test database ports by reading tracked text, and two clashed with each other and two with live listeners
incidents.rule: Allocate shared numbered resources centrally and probe the live system at use time; a text search for free numbers is not a probe
incidents.signature: Proposed numbers collided with each other and with live listeners.
incidents.root_cause: free numbers were chosen by searching text, which says nothing about what is listening now
incidents.what: several drafts proposed test database ports by reading tracked text only; two drafts chose the same number and two chose ports that a live server was already listening on; the lead read only listener listing found it, voided every proposal and allocated the numbers centrally, each a placeholder until a read only probe at that row start shows no listener

incidents.title: The first browser test to load the app config failed to link because one module was reached by two loaders
incidents.rule: Reproduce a loader failure with minimal variants before editing product code, and keep modules shared with the app config graph out of static import chains that a test runner compiles differently
incidents.signature: A module that exports a name was reported as lacking it.
incidents.root_cause: one module was loaded by two loaders in one worker, a static chain compiled one way and a dynamic graph loaded another way
incidents.what: the first browser test that loaded the app config inside the test worker failed with a missing named export error, though the module did export it; the module was reached twice, once by a static import chain that the test runner compiled as CommonJS (testing module to seed to hook) and once by the ES module graph of a dynamic config import; two minimal scratch variants with no database and no connection attempts proved it before any product edit: static seed import then dynamic config failed to link, and dynamic config alone linked and reached a later environment check; the fix moved the one value import inside the function that needs it, and a third run of the first variant after the fix linked

incidents.title: A test file was edited on order although its digest was pinned by the test authors, and the integrity gate refused the run before it started
incidents.rule: Before ordering an edit to a test file, check whether a digest manifest pins it; if it does, route the change through a successor version authored by a test author, not a direct edit.
incidents.signature: An ordered test edit made the integrity gate refuse the run before it started.
incidents.root_cause: The order did not check whether the file was pinned by a digest, and an edit by anyone but the owner cannot change pinned bytes.
incidents.what: A coordinator ordered an engineer to edit a browser test so every request sends an Origin header. The test file is pinned by a digest recorded in a manifest that the test authors own, so the edit made the approved run exit 1 at its integrity check, before any database was touched, because the active file no longer matched the pinned digest. The engineer followed the order exactly and stopped correctly.

incidents.title: A whitespace check over the branch range failed on generated SQL, while the same check on the working tree alone had passed
incidents.rule: A worktree only whitespace check is not range proof; run the check over the branch range, exclude generator output by path, never reformat it, and keep every other path clean.
incidents.signature: A worktree only check passed where the branch range check failed.
incidents.root_cause: The worktree only form does not read committed changes in the range, so it could not see the generated file.
incidents.what: A static whitespace check over the branch range exited 2 on a generated migration file, while the worktree only form had exited 0 earlier, so that earlier result was not range proof. The same class of generator output was already on the main branch in two older migration files.

incidents.title: A process guard stopped a run twice: the listing was padded with trailing spaces, and the guard's own command line matched its search
incidents.rule: A process guard normalises only trailing whitespace in process list output and searches with a self excluding pattern in a call that contains nothing else; it keeps failing closed.
incidents.signature: A guard that searches the process list failed on padding and on matching itself.
incidents.root_cause: The comparison treated padding as content, and the search pattern appeared in the line that ran it.
incidents.what: A process guard that searches the process list for a name stopped a run twice. The process list pads a command string with trailing spaces and the comparison was byte exact. The second time, the guard's own shell line contained the searched name and matched itself. Stopping was correct both times because a guard that cannot tell must fail closed.

incidents.title: Unit mutation testing on a merged change found two survivors while every named test passed
incidents.rule: A passing suite is not a discriminating suite; run cheap mutations before merge, count only runs that executed the tests, and open a follow-up change for survivors instead of reopening the merge.
incidents.signature: Mutated code passed the whole suite.
incidents.root_cause: The tests asserted outcomes but not the baseline values, and a fixture lacked the value that separates two cases.
incidents.what: Unit tier mutation testing killed seven mutations and left two alive although every named test passed. Replacing one validator with true went unseen because no unit case asserted the baseline metadata it enforces. One case could not tell root status from sibling status because its fixture supplied no sibling value. Two earlier runs were setup only and were excluded from the counts.

incidents.title: A browser test failed at its first request, and after that was fixed the next run failed at a step that had never run
incidents.rule: When a fix moves a failure later in a test, treat every newly reached step as never verified; a green earlier step proves only that step.
incidents.signature: Fixing an early test failure exposed a later step that had never run.
incidents.root_cause: The early failure stopped the test, so the later steps had never been executed and carried no evidence.
incidents.what: A browser test failed at its first API read with a 403, which hid every later step. After the fix for that cause, the next run passed login and the new identity assertion and failed where a locator for a form field was not found on the edit view, a step that had never run. The fix moved the failure later and did not finish the test.

incidents.title: A guard that blocked every network attempt logged only the API name, so a second run was needed to learn the target
incidents.rule: A blocking guard logs the API name, the full arguments and a stack trace on the first run, so one run is enough to classify the target.
incidents.signature: A blocking guard recorded what was called but not where.
incidents.root_cause: The guard recorded the call and dropped its arguments and its origin.
incidents.what: A guard that blocks every network attempt during a generator run logged only the name of the API that was called. The stop was correct but could not be classified as local inter-process communication or a remote connection. A second guarded run was authorized to log the full argument list and a stack trace per attempt.

incidents.title: A leak scanner that walked the working directory reported an ignored local file, and the push gate blocked on a file that never ships
incidents.rule: Gate a push on a scan of an export of the tracked tree; a scan of the working directory blocks on files that never ship.
incidents.signature: A scan of the working directory flagged a file outside the pushed tree.
incidents.root_cause: The scanner's input was the working directory, which holds ignored and untracked files, not the tree that a push publishes.
incidents.what: A leak scanner that scans the working directory reported an ignored local file as a leak. That file never ships, so the push gate blocked on something outside the pushed tree.

incidents.title: A push gate that piped the test run into a trimming command would have pushed even if the tests had failed
incidents.rule: Never pipe a gating command; capture its exit status first, by pipefail or by writing to a file and checking the status before reading the file.
incidents.signature: A gating command was piped, so the gate read the last command status.
incidents.root_cause: The pipeline reported the status of the last command, not of the tests.
incidents.what: A push gate was written as run the tests, pipe the output to a trimming command, and push on success. The exit status of a pipeline is the last command status, so the trimming command succeeding would have let the push run even if the tests failed. The tests passed, so nothing bad shipped.

incidents.title: Two new work item ids were minted from the current list alone, and both had already been used by merged work
incidents.rule: Before minting an id, check every place ids have ever lived (branch names, commit subjects, plan text), not only the current list; a checker that reads only the current list cannot catch reuse.
incidents.signature: A checker that read only the current list passed ids that history had already used.
incidents.root_cause: Ids were checked against the current list only, while earlier ids lived on in branch names, commit subjects and plan text.
incidents.what: A coordinator minted two new work item ids by reading only the current backlog list. Both ids had already been used by merged work, one in branch names and merge subjects and one in a regression branch. The backlog checker passed because the current list did not hold the old ids. The collision surfaced only when an engineer's branch creation failed on an existing branch name.

incidents.title: Tests added by a branch were never run before the merge, and the full suite failed on them afterwards
incidents.rule: Before a merge, the branch acceptance run must run every test file the branch adds or changes, in its own test group; a full run after the merge is a backstop, not the first execution.
incidents.signature: Tests nobody ran before the merge failed on their first execution after it.
incidents.root_cause: The branch acceptance run did not include every test file the branch added, so the first execution of some files happened after the merge.
incidents.what: A branch added tests of one kind (tests that start the whole server). The branch acceptance run covered its unit tests, its integration tests and one browser case, but not those added files, so they were never executed before the merge. The full suite after the merge was their first run. One test failed on its own fixture, because the create was refused by a size check before the assertion was reached, and a second, older test then failed too. A leftover file from the refused create is a hypothesis, not a finding.

incidents.title: A test counted a whole shared directory, and the reset reseeded into it
incidents.rule: A test that counts a shared directory or table must count only what the case creates, by baseline delta or by name, because the per-test reset and seed change the total.
incidents.signature: A total taken over a shared directory included files the case did not create.
incidents.root_cause: The assertion measured the total of shared state, which the reset and seed change, instead of what the case itself created.
incidents.what: A test snapshotted a whole shared directory and expected only the two files it created. The per-test reset reseeds a minimal record that carries its own cover file, so the directory held a third file and the case failed even when run alone. An earlier guess that a refused create left a stray file was withdrawn, because the refused create leaves nothing behind.

incidents.title: A test fixture failed an earlier check than the one under test
incidents.rule: Build a fixture that passes every guard except the one under test, and assert which guard refused; an earlier guard's refusal masks the guard the case is meant to prove.
incidents.signature: The case failed on the wrong guard, so the intended guard never ran.
incidents.root_cause: The fixture violated an earlier guard than the one under test, so that guard's refusal masked the intended one.
incidents.what: A test meant to assert that a wrong-role relation is refused used an image smaller than the role's minimum size. The size check refused the fixture create first, before the relation check was ever tried, so the case failed for the wrong reason and the guard under test was never exercised.

incidents.title: A merge checklist drafted early found a test change the merge would have broken
incidents.rule: Draft the merge acceptance checklist while the row is still open, and for each source change read the tests that assert on it, so owed test changes are found before the merge turns the full run red.
incidents.signature: A source change altered a seed record, while a unit test still asserted the old shape.
incidents.root_cause: The row changed a seed shape without a step that finds the tests asserting on it, and the whole unit tier was first due to run at the merge.
incidents.what: A branch changed its seed so the first user is created with a name and roles. A unit test on the seed still expected only an email and a password. Nobody had run the whole unit tier on the branch, so the mismatch would have surfaced as a red run after the merge. A checklist for the merge, drafted while the row was still open, predicted the failure by reading the changed source against the tests that assert on it. A second latent weakness in the same test file, report assertions not scoped to the staff key, was folded into the same repair.

incidents.title: An approval on main was not an ancestor of the branch that needed it
incidents.rule: An approval that landed on main after a branch forked is not an ancestor of that branch; merge main into the branch before any activation commit that a checker ties to that approval.
incidents.signature: A checker required the approval commit to be an ancestor of the branch head, and the branch had forked before the approval landed.
incidents.root_cause: The approval and the branch were on diverged lines of history, and the check is about ancestry, not about the approval simply existing somewhere in the repository.
incidents.what: A review approval was committed to main after a feature branch had forked from it. The identity checker ties an activation commit to its approval and requires the approval commit to be an ancestor of the activation head. The approval was not an ancestor of the branch, so an activation commit made on the branch as it stood would have been refused. The route is to merge main into the branch first, with no fast-forward, rehearsed with a merge-tree dry run, and only then make the one activation commit.

incidents.title: A setting that strips tokens from responses also stripped them from the test helper
incidents.rule: When a security setting strips tokens from responses, it strips them from local test helpers too; capture the token before the response is sanitized and assert it is present, or every downstream auth check fails at its precondition and looks like a product defect.
incidents.signature: Every auth check downstream of a local login failed, and the token was empty at the first step.
incidents.root_cause: The security setting that sanitizes responses applies to local callers too, and the probe read the token from the sanitized result.
incidents.what: A probe logged in through the framework local operation, which deletes the token from its result because the collection removes tokens from responses. The probe then sent a cookie holding the string undefined, verification failed quietly into an empty user, and the refresh cases were refused as forbidden downstream of a token that never existed. A separate direct write without a required field failed on a null constraint before its conflict update. Seven setup defects in all, and none was a product defect.

incidents.title: Static review rounds on a test harness left the same findings open
incidents.rule: When static review rounds on a harness converge slowly, run one labelled diagnostic early, on scratch state, with its result marked as neither a baseline nor an acceptance run, to learn what is really wrong.
incidents.signature: Two static passes ended with the same four findings still open.
incidents.root_cause: Reading a harness cannot show what it does when run, so each round re-derived the same open findings from text.
incidents.what: A browser walk harness went through a static review in which the reviewer found four amendments, the author applied them in place, and the recheck still left all four open after two passes. The loop was not converging fast enough for the duty that depended on it. The decision was to close the reviewer's executable gaps in one bounded pass and, in parallel, to run the harness once as a diagnostic against a scratch server and scratch database, labelled as neither a baseline nor an acceptance run, where a refusal at the binding step counts as a valid result.

incidents.title: A rule written in teammate briefs was broken by the lead in its own shell
incidents.rule: A rule written in teammate briefs binds the lead's own shell too; read your own command against the standing rules before running it, and undo any slip by its exact recorded name before any run.
incidents.signature: The author of a standing rule broke it by reflex while setting up a new work tree.
incidents.root_cause: The rule lived in the briefs written for others, and the lead's own habit ran ahead of it, with no step that checked the lead's own commands against the rules.
incidents.what: While preparing a new work tree, the lead linked the dependency directory from another tree by reflex. The standing tool rule, which the lead had pasted into every teammate brief, forbids linking dependency directories between work trees. The lead noticed the link in the next command, before any install, build or test ran, and removed it by its exact recorded name.

incidents.title: A wrapper exited zero while a step record said the step failed
incidents.rule: Gate on the step records, never on the wrapper exit status; a wrapper can exit zero while a step record says failed.
incidents.signature: The wrapper exit status was zero and one step record said failed by timeout.
incidents.root_cause: The wrapper reports that it finished, not that its steps passed, so its exit status carries no verdict on the steps.
incidents.what: A full-suite run went through a wrapper script. Every step passed up to the server integration step, which failed by its step timeout with all but two cases passed and none failed, and the smoke and browser steps never ran. The wrapper still exited zero. The step records were the truth, and they showed a run that was red by timeout only. The cause was the step budget, not a test.

incidents.title: A browser walker gathered guards over many static rounds until no allowed target could pass them
incidents.rule: When a test tool's guards are reviewed in more rounds than the tool is run, run it or simplify it; a guard that no allowed target can pass is a defect.
incidents.signature: A diagnostic run packet showed the tool could not run against any allowed target.
incidents.root_cause: Each round added a guard that was reasonable alone, and nobody checked whether the guards together left any target that could pass.
incidents.what: A browser walk harness collected a new guard in every static review round. By the sixth round it hard-coded a database name and port, required four migrations, needed a signed bindings file whose exact text nobody had sourced, and expected a fixed origin the harness could not provide. A diagnostic packet showed that no allowed target could pass its guards. The tool was parked, and its duty was split: the browser tier that runs on every full run became the regression gate, and a plain checklist click-around on a scratch server became a per-milestone report that is not a gate.

incidents.title: A successor test root was named so the identity checker could never accept it as a successor
incidents.rule: Name a successor after the family it supersedes, and read the checker's acceptance rule before writing the mapping; never loosen the gate to fit the artifact.
incidents.signature: The successor carried a name from a different family than the root it replaced.
incidents.root_cause: The name was taken from the backlog row, and the checker rule that ties a successor to a family and a higher revision had not been read before the mapping was written.
incidents.what: A successor test root was named after its backlog row. The identity checker accepts a supersession only inside one family and only with a higher revision, so a root with the row name could never replace the root it was written to replace. A reviewer found this by reading the checker source before activation. The checker was left unchanged, because a gate is never loosened to fit an artifact. The root and its coverage note were renamed into the old family with a higher revision, payload bytes unchanged, the manifest and the planned supersession lines updated, and the backlog row kept as owner.

incidents.title: An order named a scratch target without reading the guard of the command that would fill it
incidents.rule: Before naming a target in an order, read the guards of every command you name against that target.
incidents.signature: The target named in the order was on the list of targets the named command refuses.
incidents.root_cause: The order named a target and a command without reading the command guard against that target.
incidents.what: A ruling named a scratch database on the shared database server and the test seed command to fill it. That command has a guard that refuses unless the environment is marked test, both connection strings use a dedicated loopback port other than the shared one, the admin string names the maintenance database on the same port, and the database name carries a test prefix. A reviewer found the conflict while writing the checklist. The executor stopped before creating anything. The target was moved to a new dedicated cluster, the guard was left unchanged, and the order was amended so the shared server is not used at all.

incidents.title: The first real click-around found product defects that many static review rounds and every gate had missed
incidents.rule: Run the real product early and often; a cheap exploratory run beats another review round of the tool that would run it.
incidents.signature: A cheap exploratory run on a real build produced mismatches on every checklist row, within an hour of parking the strict tool.
incidents.root_cause: Review effort went into the tool that would run the product instead of into running the product.
incidents.what: After a strict browser walker was parked, a plain-checklist click-around on a real build reported mismatches against all fifteen rows. Most flows worked. It found that a seed option meant to create a minimal set had no effect and the full set was created, that a create page rendered an empty body with no input, that seeded records were published in one status field and draft in another, and that a seed report said zero media created while rows existed. Six static review rounds on the walker and every gate had found none of these. Each defect was sent to a diagnosis before any fix row, and a guess about the cause of the first stayed marked as unverified.

incidents.title: The acceptance run lacked an environment variable that the branch run and the full suite set
incidents.rule: Record the environment of every run you compare, and give the acceptance run the same environment the full suite gives.
incidents.signature: The only new failure in the acceptance run was a test that throws when one environment variable is absent.
incidents.root_cause: The acceptance run and the runs it was compared with differed in environment, and the difference was not recorded.
incidents.what: After a merge, the acceptance run showed a sixth unit failure beyond the five baseline names. The new test failed only because the acceptance script gave the unit tier no media directory variable, and the code under test throws without it. The branch run and the full suite both set it. With the variable set, the unit tier showed the same five baseline failures and no new one. The script now gives the unit tier a scratch value, as the full suite does.

incidents.title: An acceptance record was ready for signature with every test tier green while the main page of the row was blank
incidents.rule: Before signing a row that ships a page, require one observed run of that page; green test tiers alone are not acceptance for a user-facing row.
incidents.signature: Every test tier was green and a page the row ships returned a blank body.
incidents.root_cause: The acceptance evidence was test tiers alone, and none of them rendered the page the row ships.
incidents.what: An acceptance record went through four revisions and was ready for signature with every test tier green. The create page for one of the row deliverables rendered with a success status and an empty body, with no input. Only a click-around on a real build showed it. The diagnosis found that the render threw an error in the server log, because the collection enables draft autosave and the empty new draft ran a slug hook that has no source to derive from; the sibling collections without autosave rendered. The signature was held until the fix row is merged and a rerun shows the page working and a record created and edited.

incidents.title: A flag that hides the token from responses left first-user registration with an empty session cookie
incidents.rule: When a change hides or removes a credential from responses, test every flow that needs that credential to finish, not only that it is hidden.
incidents.signature: Registration returned success and stored the admin, and the browser landed on the login page.
incidents.root_cause: The flag was tested for what it hides and not for the flows that need the hidden credential to finish.
incidents.what: A hardening flag on the staff collection removes the token from auth responses. The local login operation deletes the token under that flag, and the first-user registration takes its token from that local call, so its cookie was built from a deleted token. The registration returned success, stored the admin with its roles, and set a session cookie with an empty value. The next page request sent the empty cookie and was redirected to login. Tests written for the flag proved the token absent from every response body, but nothing checked that first-user registration still signs the user in. Cookie attributes and roles were not the cause.

incidents.title: The first browser run of new end-to-end cases found two product defects that config reads and other tiers missed
incidents.rule: A config that lists a column or a field is not evidence that the page shows it or works offline; only a browser run on the real page is.
incidents.signature: A config listed a column and a field, and the real page showed neither as intended.
incidents.root_cause: Reading the config was taken as evidence of what the page shows and what it fetches, and no tier rendered the real page.
incidents.what: The first run of a set of browser cases on the real admin passed three cases and failed three. A list page silently dropped its name column, because the list view skips a group field that has no custom cell renderer, although the config listed it as a default column. An editor page requested a public content delivery host at runtime, because a read-only JSON field renders a code editor whose loader fetches from that host, although the admin must work offline. Both were product defects, not wrong oracles, so the assertions and the transport guard stayed as written.

incidents.title: The first defect of a kind prompted an audit of the whole kind, which found a second
incidents.rule: When one instance of a defect class appears, audit for the whole class before fixing only the instance.
incidents.signature: One hard-coded external host was found in a page that must work offline, and a second, silent one existed on the server.
incidents.root_cause: The first fix would have covered one instance of a class, and the class was defined by what the product may reach, not by the field that happened to be seen first.
incidents.what: A browser run found an admin editor fetching a public content delivery host, which the admin must not depend on. Instead of fixing only that field, the team ordered a static audit of every hard-coded non-local URL that an admin page or the server can reach at runtime. The audit found a second external origin: server-side telemetry that is on by default and posts to a public host at server start and on admin access, because the configuration omitted the switch that turns it off. A third origin, an avatar service, was already disabled by the configuration. The audit was a source reading, not a network observation, and said so. A unit test on the built configuration now pins the switch.

incidents.title: One load gate sized for full runs was applied to every run, and scoped runs were refused while the real load producer went unexamined
incidents.rule: Size an admission gate to the class of run it protects, and find what is actually producing the load before tightening or waiting on it.
incidents.signature: A single load threshold chosen for full-suite runs refuses small scoped runs once several teammates work in parallel.
incidents.root_cause: The gate was sized for the heaviest class of run and applied to the lightest, and the team tightened or waited on the load without first finding what produced it.
incidents.what: One load limit, sized for full-suite runs, was applied to every database and browser run. With more teammates in parallel, scoped single-row runs were refused again and again at readings only moderately above the limit, and the reds that gate each fix waited. The first admitted red was a timeout, which counts as a wasted run and not as a red. The load was then examined and found to come mostly from the system file indexer working through the installed packages of each new worktree, with several setups overlapping, not from the tests.

incidents.title: An error named only the leaf of an import chain, and a rule to add a link only when the next run named it spent a run per link
incidents.rule: When an error names only the leaf of a dependency chain, trace the chain in source and act on all of it, rather than letting each run name the next link.
incidents.signature: A load error names one package, but that package is reached through others that fail the same way.
incidents.root_cause: The rule let the error message decide what was on the path, and an error names the point of failure, not the chain that leads to it.
incidents.what: The unit tier failed before any test because the runtime refused a stylesheet file shipped by a leaf package, reached through a framework export that a generated map had begun to import. The first ruling allowed only the packages in the failing chain to be added to the runner inline list, and another only if the next run named it. The error named only the leaf, so each further link would have cost one run. A search of installed source showed that the export re-exports a UI package whose client index also imports the stylesheet.

incidents.title: An implementer was assigned after checking only who wrote the test payload, and the root also held a coverage statement the implementer had written
incidents.rule: An author-conflict check covers every file of the root, including coverage statements and approval markers, by log and a name search, before the assignment is sent; the implementer own check stays as the second line.
incidents.signature: An author-conflict check was run on one file of a root, and a different file of the same root named the assignee as author.
incidents.root_cause: The check was scoped to the file most obviously authored, not to every file of the root, so coverage statements and approval markers were left out.
incidents.what: The lead assigned an implementer to an early row after checking only that the implementer had not authored the test payload. The root also contained a coverage statement that the implementer had written. The implementer ran its own check, found its name on that file, and stopped. The coverage statement was ruled to be part of the root, and the row was reassigned to another implementer with the same author and reviewer check.

incidents.title: A brief stated a baseline environment from a compacted summary, and the baseline script showed the opposite
incidents.rule: State a baseline environment from the script or log that produced it, never from memory; an implementer who sees a premise contradict the artifact follows the artifact and reports it.
incidents.signature: A brief says a baseline ran with a variable unset, and the script that produced the baseline sets it.
incidents.root_cause: An environment fact was carried from a summary into an instruction instead of being read from the script or log that produced the baseline.
incidents.what: A brief said a whole-suite baseline had been run with a storage variable unset and that this gave exactly the known failures. The premise came from a compacted summary. The implementer read the script that produced the baseline, found the variable was set to a fresh directory, and saw that the failure names did not involve that variable. It followed the artifact and reported the contradiction. The wording was withdrawn, and every comparison was ruled to set the variable to a fresh directory the runner creates and records.

incidents.title: A branch scrubbed a local path in a later commit, and a range scan found it still in history
incidents.rule: Scan every commit of a range, not only the final tree, before merging anything that will be pushed; a scrub in a later commit does not clean history.
incidents.signature: The final tree passes a leak scan, and a scan of every commit of the range does not.
incidents.root_cause: A final-tree check was treated as covering history, but a later commit that removes a value does not remove it from earlier commits.
incidents.what: Intermediate commits of a branch added a local home path to an evidence document, and a later commit removed it. The final tree was clean. A scan of the whole range found the path in history, and a plain merge would have carried those commits into the history that is pushed. The branch was landed as a squash whose tree equalled the merge result.

incidents.title: A run command silently dropped a named option, and three tests that ran it asserted only things that are true for the full data set too
incidents.rule: A test that exercises an option goes through the real entry point and asserts an observable effect that differs with and without the option; exit 0 and side markers are not evidence the option took effect.
incidents.signature: A test runs a command with an option and asserts exit status, timing and a side marker, all of which hold with or without the option.
incidents.root_cause: The tests checked that the command ran, not what it produced, and the one test aimed at the option bypassed the entry point where the option was lost.
incidents.what: A framework run command rebuilt the script argument list from positional arguments only, so a named option was dropped before the script saw it, and the full data set loaded instead of the minimal one. Three tests ran that command and asserted exit status, timing records and the presence of one user, all true for the full set as well. A fourth test called the function directly and skipped the entry point.

incidents.title: Two fields claimed the same publication state, and the seed wrote only one, so the admin and the public predicate disagreed
incidents.rule: When two fields can claim one state, derive one from the other or assert both in the same test, and write through the framework supported transition.
incidents.signature: An application status says published and the framework draft status says draft for the same record.
incidents.root_cause: Nothing tied the two fields together, and the seed wrote one directly instead of using the framework transition that sets both.
incidents.what: An application status field and the framework own draft status both claimed to say whether a record is published. The seed wrote the application status as published and never set the framework status, so the admin showed drafts with a publish action while the public predicate, which reads only the application status, matched the same records. The database held rows with the pair published and draft, and rows with draft and draft.

incidents.title: An independence rule did not say what counts as an agent or as a part, and four of nine parallel slices stopped at once
incidents.rule: Define independence per agent instance, and name which artifacts block (wrote the test or judged its cases) and which only need disclosure (inventories, citation audits).
incidents.signature: A rule says to stop if you authored or reviewed any part, and different agents read part and agent differently.
incidents.root_cause: The rule used broad words and left the unit of independence and the list of blocking artifacts undefined.
incidents.what: An independence rule said to stop if you authored or reviewed any part of a root, without defining either term. One agent counted a different agent that ran on the same model as itself. Others counted a coverage-citation audit or a census table. Four of nine parallel slices stopped at once. The clarified rule is per agent instance, blocks on writing the test or judging its cases, and only requires disclosure for inventories, citation audits, allocation audits and compatibility proposals.

incidents.title: A build step was given the load threshold meant for timing-sensitive runs and was refused twice while the host was busy
incidents.rule: Pick each step load threshold by whether its result depends on timing; a build that only gets slower uses the looser class.
incidents.signature: A strict admission threshold designed for timing-sensitive runs is applied to a step whose result does not depend on timing.
incidents.root_cause: The threshold was chosen by the kind of tool being run, not by whether the result depends on timing.
incidents.what: The lead gave a build step the strict load threshold that exists for timing-sensitive browser runs. The host was busy with unrelated work, and the build was refused twice. A build does not depend on timing and only gets slower under load, so the strict class protected nothing and delayed the work.

incidents.title: An agent reported a background run as running from its launch, but the task had only echoed a prompt and no test process existed
incidents.rule: Report a run as running only from its own output (a launch line, a PID that exists); a started task is not a started run.
incidents.signature: A background task exists and a launch was acknowledged, but no process of the run exists.
incidents.root_cause: The report was based on the launch of the wrapper task, not on output of the run itself.
incidents.what: An agent reported a background run as admitted and running from its launch. The task had only echoed an interactive prompt, and no test process existed. The agent found this on its own recheck and corrected the report. A started task had been taken for a started run.

incidents.title: Mutation restore receipts were kept only in tool output, so two independent reviewers could not verify restoration
incidents.rule: A mutation run keeps a receipt per mutant, the diff and the hash after restore, as a file before the scratch copy is deleted; tool output is not evidence a second reviewer can check.
incidents.signature: A reviewer asks for proof that a mutated file was restored, and the only record is output that was not saved.
incidents.root_cause: Restoration was treated as a step to perform, not as a fact to leave evidence of.
incidents.what: For two slices the restore receipts of the mutation runs existed only as tool output, with no file kept, and two reviewers held on the same gap. The gap was accepted because the retained logs showed distinct assertion failures, and each reviewer had matched the shipped file to the committed blob and seen a passing run on it. From then on every mutant writes a file with its diff and the hash after restore before the scratch copy is deleted.

incidents.title: A harness test failed because another run's orphan database vanished mid-test, so the test depended on state it did not own
incidents.rule: A test must not assert on state it did not create; compare only the names the test itself made.
incidents.signature: A cleanliness assertion over a shared server sees a resource disappear between its baseline and its end.
incidents.root_cause: The test took a baseline over shared state and so depended on every other run leftovers.
incidents.what: In the second full-suite run one harness step failed: a cleanliness assertion saw a test database vanish between its baseline and its end. That database was an orphan of the previous run, which had timed out, and it was removed during the second run, most likely by the garbage collection the test exercises. The red was environmental and not a code defect. A second orphan remained and was reported and left in place.

incidents.title: Read-once-and-refuse load admission stopped whole teammate cycles while load spiked and fell within a minute
incidents.rule: When load is spiky, admit by waiting for the gate with a bounded timeout and a printed admitting reading, not by one reading at launch.
incidents.signature: A launch is refused on one load reading, and the next reading a minute later would have admitted it.
incidents.root_cause: Admission was a single sample of a signal that varies faster than the cycle it gates.
incidents.what: A once-at-launch load reading refused scoped runs, and each refusal ended the teammate whole cycle, although load spiked and fell within a minute. A helper now waits up to fifteen minutes until the load is under the class limit, prints the admitting reading and exits with a distinct code on timeout. The limits per class are unchanged, and the printed line is the admission evidence.

incidents.title: An activation moved a superseded root's spec while main carried the approved successor edge, and identity failed only after the merge
incidents.rule: Before activating a root, confirm on current main that it is still the terminal of its supersession chain; run the identity check after merging main into the branch, not only before.
incidents.signature: An identity check reports a missing deletion of a pending copy after a branch merges a main that supersedes the activated revision.
incidents.root_cause: The activation checked the revision against the branch view, not against the supersession chain on current main.
incidents.what: An activation moved the spec of one revision of a test root to its active destination. Main then carried the approved edge from that revision to a later one, so the activated revision was no longer the terminal. The identity check on the branch tip after merging main failed on the superseded pending copy and was found only after the merge. The branch now activates the terminal revision, with no root bytes or manifest edited.

incidents.title: An implementer proposed editing a pinned root's mock to fit a new helper contract, and the fix was a wrapper that kept the mocked shape
incidents.rule: When a new contract collides with a pinned test mock, keep the mocked function return shape and add a new function or wrapper for the new contract; change the test only through a successor root authored by someone else.
incidents.signature: A new return contract is incompatible with a pinned test's mock, and the proposed fix edits the pinned file.
incidents.root_cause: The new contract was fitted to the product helper first and the pinned test double was then expected to follow.
incidents.what: An implementer asked to change the return value of a mock in an activated test root so that it fits a new helper return contract. The file was bound by the root manifest, so the edit would fail the identity check, and an implementer may not edit a root. The first choice was to leave the return shape of every mocked function unchanged and carry the new fields in a new function or wrapper called only by the seed module. Only if that cannot work does another author write a successor root with the mechanical change.

incidents.title: A rulings file grew past what a reader's tool returns, and a read of a named range was clipped, so compliance could not be certified
incidents.rule: Do not require a read whose size exceeds what the reader tool returns; name the exact sections to read, and treat an unnamed old section as outside the compliance check.
incidents.signature: An instruction requires reading a range of a file whose size exceeds what the reader tool returns.
incidents.root_cause: A read requirement was written for a file that kept growing, with no bound on what the reader could actually receive.
incidents.what: The file of lead rulings grew past 660 KB, and a teammate reported that its read of a named range of rulings was clipped. An instruction to read the whole range could not be certified as followed. From then on a brief names the rulings to read, they are read by heading together with the standing rules quoted in the brief, and missing an unnamed old ruling is not a compliance failure.

incidents.title: Backlog rows stayed open after their fixes merged, so the backlog no longer showed what was done
incidents.rule: Update a backlog row status with the merge commit at the time its fix merges, so the backlog stays the record of what is done.
incidents.signature: The backlog lists as open rows whose fixes are already on the main line.
incidents.root_cause: Marking a row done was a separate step from the merge, with no check tying the two together.
incidents.what: Six backlog rows whose fixes had already merged were still open. A plan update was assigned to set each status with its merge commit, and the backlog check must pass. The backlog is the record of what is done, and it stops being that record when merged work is not marked.

incidents.title: Two reviewers were named who had written or judged the roots they were to review, and both stopped at the author check
incidents.rule: Before naming a reviewer, read the root coverage author line and review history; the reviewer own author check is the second line, not the first.
incidents.signature: A reviewer is named without reading the root author line and review history, and the reviewer author check refuses.
incidents.root_cause: The assignment relied on the reviewer own check as the only author check.
incidents.what: Two reviews were assigned to teammates who had written or judged the root of the slice under review. Both stopped at their own author check, which was correct. The reviews were reassigned, and the assigner now reads the root coverage author line and its review history before naming a reviewer.

incidents.title: A landing tool read a bare file name as a test-root name, so a file was left out of a landing and the identifier check failed
incidents.rule: A tool that accepts both root names and file paths must not guess which one a bare token is; list what it will land and compare with what was intended before it runs.
incidents.signature: A tool accepts root names and file paths, and a bare file name is taken as a root name.
incidents.root_cause: The tool guessed the kind of a bare token instead of requiring an explicit form.
incidents.what: A landing tool took a bare file name given for the backlog as the name of a test root. The backlog file was therefore not landed as a file, and the identifier check failed. The curator assignment records the cause as a bare file name read as a root name.

incidents.title: A root was passed to a landing helper by name and by path, and the cleanup removed a file twice and stopped
incidents.rule: Give a landing helper each item once and in its one documented form; an item named twice is a cleanup that can fail halfway.
incidents.signature: The same item is given to a helper in two forms, and a later step acts on it twice.
incidents.root_cause: The helper did not de-duplicate an item that reached it in two forms.
incidents.what: A pending root was passed to the landing helper both by its bare name and by its coverage path. The cleanup step removed the same file twice and stopped halfway, and the landing was finished by hand. The rule is to pass a pending root by its bare name only.

incidents.title: A manifest listed its lines unsorted and the landing gate refused it
incidents.rule: Run the landing gate own identity check on a root before handing it over, so a mechanical ordering rule is met by the author and not found at the landing.
incidents.signature: The identity check requires sorted manifest lines, and a manifest lists one group before another.
incidents.root_cause: The ordering rule was checked only at the landing and not by the author before handing the root over.
incidents.what: The manifest of one root listed its unit lines before its end-to-end lines. The identity check requires sorted lines, so the root was not landed with the rest of its batch, and the author was assigned to sort it.

incidents.title: Three unit tests timed out at a short child-process bound under parallel load and passed in isolation
incidents.rule: A short child-process bound fails under parallel load while the test is correct; classify such a timeout by an isolated rerun, and give child-process tests a bound that tolerates the load class they run in.
incidents.signature: Tests that spawn a child process fail with a spawn timeout at a five-second bound only while the host is loaded.
incidents.root_cause: A short fixed bound on child-process tests assumes an idle host.
incidents.what: In an acceptance run of the whole unit tier, eight tests failed: the five known baseline cases and three new ones, all spawn timeouts at a five-second bound, in fixtures that use a temporary root and do not depend on the repository. Rerun alone after waiting for the load to fall under the class limit, the two files passed. The acceptance was ruled equal to the baseline apart from the known timeout class under load.

incidents.title: A helper script was edited in place while another process was executing it, and that run died with a syntax error at a shifted line
incidents.rule: Never rewrite a script in place while any process may run it; write a new file and switch names, and quote the helper hash in the evidence that used it.
incidents.signature: A script that other threads run is rewritten in place, and a running shell fails at a line number that no longer matches.
incidents.root_cause: A shared helper was treated as editable like any file, though other threads execute it while it is edited.
incidents.what: A comparison script was edited in place while a process was executing it. The shell reads a script by file offset as it runs, so an inserted line shifts the rest. The first time the exact bytes were restored within seconds, before the process read past its current command. The second time another thread comparison died with a syntax error at a shifted line and was not evidence. The helpers are now read-only, a change is a new file name announced in a ruling, and reports quote the helper hash.

incidents.title: Three test roots by three authors used the same guessed locator for a generated field that the installed library does not render
incidents.rule: Do not guess a locator for a generated field; cite the installed source line that renders it, and when one guess is found, audit every root for the same guess.
incidents.signature: Several browser tests scope a generated field by a role or label that its library never renders.
incidents.root_cause: Locators were written from how the field should look, not from the source that renders it.
incidents.what: Three browser roots by three authors scoped a generated upload field with a group role or one of two guessed button labels. The installed source renders the field as a plain element with an id built from its path, with a fixed button label from the installed translations, shown only while the field has no value. One pattern was set for every generated upload field, bound to a cited source line. A capture showed that generated group fields also lack a group role.

incidents.title: A root named a mutation its assertions could not see, because the next line returned the same status
incidents.rule: A mutation named as a case witness must be one the assertions can see; trace what the next line returns before naming it, and state the expected red line.
incidents.signature: The named mutation is removed, and the case still passes because a later line refuses the same way.
incidents.root_cause: The witness was chosen from the line mutated, not from what the following lines return.
incidents.what: A root coverage named as its witness a mutation that removes an early return for a missing sniffed type. With no sniffed type, the next line, which compares the declared type with the sniffed one, is true, so the code still refuses with the same status and the case stays green. The witness was ruled to be a mutation the case can see, such as disabling the whole refusal so the bad bytes are stored, stated with its expected red line.

incidents.title: A feedback check accepted any visible alert on the page, so a stale alert could satisfy it
incidents.rule: A feedback assertion must fail without the action under test: assert the element is absent before the action and present after it, on a fresh page and scoped to the field, never on any alert on the page.
incidents.signature: An assertion looks for any visible alert, and an alert from earlier or from another field satisfies it.
incidents.root_cause: The assertion tested the presence of an alert and not the change caused by the action.
incidents.what: A root check for refusal feedback accepted any visible alert element. An alert already on the page, or one belonging to another field, could satisfy it. Each refusal now asserts that no matching error element is present before submission and one is present after the response, on a fresh form, and the field-specific case binds to that field scope with a named product mutation that moves or removes its error.

incidents.title: A reviewer was named after checking commit authorship only, and the reviewer had judged the root's cases in an earlier review file
incidents.rule: An author-conflict check covers review files as well as commits: search both for the root identifier and read the author of every hit before the reviewer is named.
incidents.signature: An author-conflict check covers commits, and the conflict is in a review file.
incidents.root_cause: The author check was defined over commits, and a review is authorship of a judgement that lives in a different file.
incidents.what: A reviewer was named for a slice after checking commit authorship but not review files. The reviewer had written an earlier review file that judged the cases of the slice root, so it stopped at its own author check, which was correct. The assigner now searches the review folder for the root identifier and reads the author of each hit for every candidate before naming a reviewer.

incidents.title: An absence check for a hidden field matched the hidden input the library renders, so a regression root was red on unchanged code
incidents.rule: A regression root must be green on unchanged code before any mutation; an absence selector for a hidden field must account for the hidden input the library still renders.
incidents.signature: A test asserts that a selector for a hidden field matches nothing, and the library renders a hidden input with the field id.
incidents.root_cause: The absence check was written from what a hidden field should mean, not from what the library renders.
incidents.what: The activation run of a regression root on unchanged code failed both cases at an assertion that a selector for a hidden field, a JSON field or an editor widget matches zero elements, receiving one. The runner stopped before any mutation and weakened nothing. Installed source shows the library renders a hidden field as a hidden input with an id built from the field path, so the single match was the product working as intended. The selector arm for the field id was a root defect. The earlier static review could not see this, since it needs the rendered markup.

incidents.title: A fix gave a list column a custom cell and dropped the default cell's link to the record, so the list lost its only way to open a record
incidents.rule: Replacing a framework default cell, field or component replaces everything it did, not only what the change targeted; list what the default provided before replacing it, and test it.
incidents.signature: A custom cell component replaces the default cell, and the default cell carried the record link.
incidents.root_cause: The change targeted one behavior, display, and replaced a component that also provided navigation.
incidents.what: A fix for localized display gave the first list column a custom cell component. Installed source shows that a field with a custom cell is rendered through it and the default cell, which carries the link to the record, is never used. The custom cell returns a plain span, so the list lost the link from a row to its editor. The link was ruled required admin behavior. The regression root does not assert it, because it must be green on the current code. A new row owns the link, with a root red by design, and a later fix must keep both the link and the localized display.

incidents.title: A full run stopped at the unit step because one test hit the runner's default five-second bound while host load rose sevenfold
incidents.rule: A per-test bound left at the runner default is a decision nobody made; set it at the project level for the load class the step runs in, and treat a default-bound timeout under load as a wasted run, not a red.
incidents.signature: A unit test fails with a timeout at the runner's default bound, and the host load at the end of the step is many times that at its start.
incidents.root_cause: The per-test bound was never chosen for the project, so the runner default applied to a test that takes seconds under load.
incidents.what: In a full run the unit step passed all but one test, so it exited 1 and the integration, server and smoke steps did not run. The failure was a test that loads the sanitized configuration, timing out at the runner's default per-test bound while the load average rose from about 13 to about 95 during the step. The unit project set no timeout. One implementer change set a 30-second per-test bound in the unit project block, accepting that a hung unit test now fails at 30 seconds.

incidents.title: An icon-only button had no accessible name, so a role-name locator could never match and the test timed out
incidents.rule: Before writing a role-name locator for a control, read the installed source for its accessible name; an icon-only control with no label has none, and a test that waits for one can only time out.
incidents.signature: A test waits for a button by role and name, and the button has no name to match.
incidents.root_cause: The locator assumed every button has an accessible name.
incidents.what: A browser root located the remove control of an upload field by its role and a name pattern, and the run timed out at that line. Installed source shows the control is an icon-only button with no children, no aria-label and no tooltip, and the button component sets an aria-label only from its prop. A role-name pattern cannot match it. The successor binds it by class inside the field scope and also handles the empty field, where no remove control exists.

incidents.title: A graceful pause worked because each in-flight teammate finished one step, wrote a checkpoint and left its workspace as it was
incidents.rule: To pause a team safely, tell each in-flight teammate to finish only the current step, write a resume checkpoint, and leave its worktree and processes as they are; resume from those checkpoints and never redo finished work.
incidents.signature: A team stops on request and resumes later, and every member continues from its own recorded state.
incidents.root_cause: Not a failure: a pause that is bounded to one step per member and records the state needed to continue.
incidents.what: When the owner asked for a graceful pause, no new job, run, merge or review started. In-flight teammates were told to finish the current step only, append a pause checkpoint to their report, keep their worktree and database cluster as they were, and stop. Idle teammates got no new work, and shared services were not touched. On the resume message every teammate continued from its own checkpoint and an in-flight slice was continued, with no finished work restarted.

incidents.title: Test roots imported helpers by paths anchored at their pending depth, so every import would break at the active destination
incidents.rule: Check that every import of a root resolves from the path where the file will run, not only from where it is written; a pending copy that must move byte-identical cannot be repaired at activation.
incidents.signature: A spec imports by relative paths that resolve from its pending folder and climb outside the repository from its active folder.
incidents.root_cause: The paths were written for where the file sits while it is a draft, not for where it will run.
incidents.what: The specs of two roots imported helpers and a testing module with relative paths written for the pending folder. At the active destination those paths climb outside the repository and every import target is absent. Activation must copy a pending file byte for byte, so an activator may not rewrite the imports, and a valid manifest does not prove that imports resolve. Both roots were blocked and successors were assigned.

incidents.title: A named mutant was masked by an independent guard upstream, so the case could never turn red for the stated reason
incidents.rule: Before naming a mutation as a case witness, trace every independent guard on the path from the mutated line to the assertion; a second guard masks the mutant.
incidents.signature: A mutation weakens one access setting, and a separate guard on the same path still refuses.
incidents.root_cause: The witness was chosen from the setting that sounds related, without tracing the other guards on the path.
incidents.what: A root coverage proposed making a collection publicly readable as the witness mutation for a case that visits an admin route. Installed source shows the admin route is first guarded by an access check that sends an unauthenticated visitor to the login route, independently of the collection read setting. The mutation leaves that guard intact and the case stays green. The reviewer required a witness that reaches the route guard without weakening the case, and noted that a wait timeout on the redirect is not by itself the requested assertion red.

incidents.title: A configuration mutation failed a setup assertion before any case oracle ran, so the red proved nothing about the cases
incidents.rule: A mutation counts for a case only when it fails at that case own assertion; check that the setup and fixture assertions do not fail first.
incidents.signature: A mutation breaks the configuration, and the shared setup asserts the same configuration and fails first.
incidents.root_cause: The mutation target overlapped the fixture assertion, so the earliest failure was the setup one.
incidents.what: A root coverage named removing or reordering collections in the configuration as the mutations for two cases. The setup step of the root asserts exactly the same list of collections, so those mutations fail in setup before the dashboard cards or the navigation are checked. A setup assertion is not evidence that each case detects broken rendered links. The reviewer required mutations that survive setup and reach the case assertions, and ruled that discovery, import or setup failure is not mutation evidence.

incidents.title: A standing promise to guard every proven behavior had no inventory, so partial protection could pass as coverage
incidents.rule: Turn a broad protection promise into a per-item inventory with strict status definitions, a count, and a proposed guard for every gap; partial protection of a row is a gap.
incidents.signature: A broad request such as never break what already works is acknowledged but never turned into a per-item count of what is guarded.
incidents.root_cause: The request was a principle with no measure, so each new test looked like progress while the uncovered share stayed invisible.
incidents.what: The standing request was that every behavior a manual walk proves gets an automated guard. A reviewer turned it into a static map with one line per checklist row. Each line recorded whether the guard was active in a collected test path, approved but pending, under review, blocked on a reviewed defect, or missing. Of 46 lines, 9 were active, 1 approved, 4 under review, 8 blocked and 24 had none. Each gap got a proposed root, grouped into 20 proposals. Active meant a matching assertion existed, not that a mutation had been shown to kill it, and a row with an essential uncovered behavior counted as missing even if partial protection existed.

incidents.title: A one-line comment conflict hid a type break from the automatic part of the merge
